_meta.purpose: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A in CatalogFile shape, so applyCatalogFile creates the framework, its 93 requirements, the 93 control templates, their requirement links and the pack together.
_meta.why: The templates were generated inline inside prisma/seed.ts, which is not run on production deploys — so a fresh database or a restore gets none of them. Production has them only because a one-off backfill put them there. This is also the precondition for authoring: the generated templates carried GENERIC_TEMPLATE_TASKS and there was nowhere for authored content to live.
_meta.grounding: Requirement keys, titles, summaries and themes carried over verbatim from prisma/fixtures/iso27001_2022_annexA.json. Task content is authored from each control's own title and its 25-60 character intent paraphrase — the only grounding Annex A carries here. No ISO text is quoted or reproduced. Authored against docs/control-task-authoring.md, whose own worked example is A.8.24, an Annex A control with the same thin grounding.
_meta.join: Template A-<key> links to requirement <key>; 93 of 93 resolve by construction.
_meta.packKey: ISO27001_2022_BASE — the key production already has, carrying all 93 templates. seed.ts spells it the same way, so this framework adds no pack-key divergence.

templates.title: Policies for information security
templates.description: Establish and maintain information security policy framework

title.en: List the security topics that require a policy statement, and which policy covers each

description.en: Work from the organisation's activities, its legal and contractual obligations and the risks it has accepted to derive the topics on which a written position has to exist. Mark each topic as covered by an existing policy, covered only in part, or not covered at all. Attach the topic list showing the covering policy or the gap against every entry.

evidenceHint.en: Topic list with the covering policy, partial coverage or gap recorded against each topic

title.en: Have management approve the top-level information security policy

description.en: Produce a single statement giving the purpose and scope of information security in the organisation, the principles it works to, and the topic policies it governs, and put it to the person or body holding the authority to approve it. Attach the approved document showing who approved it and on what date.

evidenceHint.en: The approved top-level policy showing its approver and approval date

title.en: Record the owner, approver, audience and review trigger for every policy in the set

description.en: For each policy on the topic list capture in one register the owner, the approving authority, the current version and its approval date, the audience the policy binds, and what causes it to be reviewed — an elapsed interval, a change of obligation, an incident, or a combination. Attach the register with one row per policy.

evidenceHint.en: Policy register, one row per policy, carrying owner, version, audience and review trigger

title.en: Issue each new and revised policy version to the audience the register names

description.en: When a policy is first approved or reissued, put the current version where the audience recorded against it can obtain it and tell that audience it has changed, including contractors and third-party personnel where the policy binds them. Attach the issue record for every version released in the period, naming the audience told, the date, and where the current version can be obtained.

evidenceHint.en: Issue record per policy version: audience told, date, and where the current version is available

title.en: Review each policy whose review trigger has fired and record the outcome

description.en: Take every policy the register shows as due, check whether it still matches current practice, obligations and risk, and record for each whether it was reissued unchanged, amended, merged into another policy or withdrawn, together with who approved that outcome. Attach the review record and the register rows updated as a result.

evidenceHint.en: Per-policy review record with the outcome and its approver, plus the updated register rows

templates.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
templates.description: Define and assign information security roles

title.en: Break the organisation's security work into responsibilities somebody must hold

description.en: Go through the security work the organisation depends on — protecting information, deciding and accepting risk, maintaining the policies and procedures, handling security events, overseeing the parties acting for the organisation — and write each discrete responsibility as one line saying what its holder actually does. Attach the responsibility list.

evidenceHint.en: Responsibility list, each entry with a one-line statement of what its holder does

title.en: Assign every responsibility to a named holder, with the date the assignment took effect

description.en: Against each entry on the list record the person or named role that holds it and the date the assignment took effect. No entry may be left without a holder — that is the whole point of the record. Where the organisation has arranged cover for the holder's absence, or a point at which the holder refers a decision upward rather than taking it alone, record that against the entry as well; where the size or shape of the organisation means there is neither, record that fact against the entry rather than leaving the row incomplete. Attach the completed assignment record.

evidenceHint.en: Assignment record with a named holder and effective date on every row, and the cover or escalation arrangement recorded where one exists

title.en: Write the assigned responsibilities into the definition of each role that carries them

description.en: For every role named in the assignment record, add the security responsibilities it now holds to that role's own definition, so the obligation attaches to the post rather than to whoever currently occupies it. Attach the amended role definitions.

evidenceHint.en: Amended role definitions naming the security responsibilities each role carries

title.en: Update the assignment record for each responsibility that changed holder this period

description.en: For every responsibility whose holder or deputy changed during the period — whoever the employment event belonged to — amend the assignment record to name the incoming holder and the date the responsibility moved, and list any responsibility the change left with no holder at all. Attach the amended rows together with the list of unheld responsibilities, empty if there are none.

evidenceHint.en: The assignment rows amended this period, plus the list of responsibilities left unheld

title.en: Reconcile the assignment record against who actually works here now

description.en: Compare every named holder and deputy against current personnel records and current role definitions, and list the responsibilities now held by someone who has left or moved, held by a role that no longer exists, or held by nobody at all. Attach the reconciliation with the resolution recorded against each discrepancy.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing orphaned, vacant or misassigned responsibilities and how each was resolved

title.en: Identify the duty pairs that must not be held by one person

description.en: Walk the processes that move money, grant access, change production systems and handle sensitive data, and record each pair of duties that would let one person act and conceal it — requesting versus approving access, developing versus deploying, raising versus approving payment. Attach the conflicting-duties list with the process each pair sits in.

evidenceHint.en: The conflicting-duties list, one row per pair with its process

title.en: Map each conflicting duty pair to the system roles and permissions that grant it

description.en: For every pair on the list, identify in each in-scope system the concrete roles, groups or permissions that confer each side, so the conflict becomes testable against an entitlement export. Attach the mapping from duty pair to role or permission per system.

evidenceHint.en: The duty-pair to role/permission mapping, per system

title.en: Separate the accounts that currently hold both sides of a conflicting pair

description.en: Run the mapping against current entitlements, identify accounts holding both sides, and remove or move one side for each so no single account retains the conflict. Attach the before and after entitlement export for the accounts changed.

evidenceHint.en: Before/after entitlement export for every account changed

title.en: Record a compensating check for each conflict that cannot be separated

description.en: Where headcount or system design makes separation impossible, record the conflict, why it persists, the detective check that compensates (independent review of a log, second-person confirmation of the output), who performs it, and who accepted the residual risk. Attach the exception record.

evidenceHint.en: The exception record, each entry naming its compensating check and risk acceptor

title.en: Test current entitlements for accounts holding both sides of a conflicting pair

description.en: Re-run the duty-pair mapping over a fresh entitlement export from each in-scope system, list the violations found, and record the remediation or the exception each was closed under. Attach the check output and the remediation record.

evidenceHint.en: The check output listing violating accounts, with the resolution of each

title.en: List the groups of people who act for the organisation and the manager answerable for each

description.en: Enumerate the populations doing work for or on behalf of the organisation — employees by function, fixed-term and temporary staff, contractors, and third-party personnel given accounts or premises access — and name for each the manager who answers for that group's conduct toward information security. Attach the list with an answerable manager against every group.

evidenceHint.en: Group list with a named answerable manager for every population, contractors and third-party personnel included

title.en: Write and issue the brief setting out what a manager must do about security

description.en: Set down what management requires of every manager: tell each person joining or transferring into their team which policies and procedures bind their work before access is granted, make the time and means available for the security work their people are required to do, answer what those people cannot resolve themselves, and pass unresolved refusal to comply to the route the organisation has defined for it. Approve the brief and issue it to every manager on the group list. Attach the approved brief and the record of who has been issued with it.

evidenceHint.en: The approved manager brief plus the issue record naming each manager and the date

title.en: Record that each new or transferring person was told which rules bind their work before they got access

description.en: For every person starting in or moving into a team during the period, capture the manager's confirmation of what they were told applies to their work and the date it was given, then set that date against the date their access was granted. Attach the confirmations for the period with any that came after the access grant flagged.

evidenceHint.en: Per-person confirmations for the period showing briefing date and access-grant date, with late ones flagged

title.en: Log what people raised as unable to comply with, and the decision management gave back

description.en: Keep the record of every case where a person told their manager they could not do what the rules require — the work would stop, the equipment does not permit it, a customer forbids it — with what was asked, who decided, what was decided, and when the answer was given back. A nil return is a valid entry where nothing was raised. Attach the log.

evidenceHint.en: Log of matters raised in the period, or a nil return, each with the decision, the decider and the date answered

title.en: Sample teams and check the manager did what the brief requires of them

description.en: Take a sample of the groups on the list and for each look for the briefing confirmations covering its recent starters and movers and the answers given back on anything its people raised. Record where the manager's acts were missing, late or undocumented, and what was done about it. Attach the sample review.

evidenceHint.en: Sample review naming the teams examined, the omissions found and the action taken on each

title.en: Identify the authorities the organisation must be able to reach

description.en: Name the regulators, data protection authority, law enforcement, national CERT and sector bodies relevant to where the organisation operates and what it processes, and record for each what circumstance would require contacting it. Attach the authority list with the trigger per entry.

evidenceHint.en: The authority list, each entry with the circumstance that triggers contact

title.en: Record the current reporting channel and any reference numbers for each authority

description.en: For every authority on the list capture the channel actually used (portal, hotline, secure email), any registration or case reference the organisation already holds, and the internal person authorised to make contact. Attach the contact register.

evidenceHint.en: The authority contact register, one row per authority

title.en: Write the procedure for contacting an authority during a security incident

description.en: State who decides that contact is required, who makes it, what information is provided, how legal review fits in, and how the contact is recorded. Cross-reference the incident procedure so the two do not diverge. Attach the approved procedure.

evidenceHint.en: The approved authority-contact procedure

title.en: Log every contact made with an authority and what was reported

description.en: Record each outbound and inbound contact: date, authority, who made it, the subject, what information was disclosed, and the response or reference number received. Attach the contact log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: The authority contact log, one entry per contact with subject and outcome

title.en: Verify each register entry against the authority's currently published channel

description.en: Check every entry still resolves — portal reachable, address and telephone current, named internal contact still in post — and correct the entries that have moved. Attach the verification record showing the date each entry was confirmed and what changed.

evidenceHint.en: The verification record, confirmation date and correction per entry

templates.title: Contact with special interest groups
templates.description: Maintain contacts with security forums and groups

title.en: Identify the security forums and professional groups relevant to the organisation

description.en: List the sector information-sharing groups, vendor security communities, national CERT distribution lists and professional associations that match the technologies the organisation runs and the sector it operates in, and record what each is expected to provide. Attach the list with the expected benefit per entry.

evidenceHint.en: The candidate group list, each with the benefit expected from it

title.en: Enrol in the selected groups and name the person who represents the organisation

description.en: Complete membership or subscription for each group chosen from the list, and record the named representative, an alternate, and the joining date. Attach the membership register and the confirmations of membership.

evidenceHint.en: The membership register showing group, representative, alternate and joining date

title.en: Set the rules for what may be shared with these groups

description.en: Record what information about incidents, vulnerabilities, architecture and customers may leave the organisation through these channels, at what classification, in what form (anonymised or attributed), and who approves an exception. Attach the approved sharing rules.

evidenceHint.en: The approved sharing rules for special interest group participation

title.en: Circulate advisories received from these groups to the teams that must act

description.en: For each advisory, bulletin or alert received through a membership, route it to the owning team and record what was sent, to whom and on what date. Attach the distribution record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: The distribution record, item received with date and recipient team

title.en: Assess each membership for what it returned and decide whether to keep it

description.en: For every group in the register, record what was received during the period, what action it triggered, and whether participation met the benefit recorded when it was selected; recommend retain, drop or replace. Attach the review with a decision per group.

evidenceHint.en: The membership review, with a retain/drop/replace decision per group

title.en: List the threat intelligence sources the organisation will draw on

description.en: Record each feed, vendor bulletin, CERT advisory, commercial service and community source to be used, what level it covers (strategic, tactical or operational), how it is accessed, and its cost. Attach the source list with coverage per source.

evidenceHint.en: The intelligence source list, each with coverage level and access route

title.en: Record the technologies and services incoming intelligence is filtered against

description.en: Derive from the asset inventory the products, platforms, cloud services and business services the organisation actually runs, so an incoming item can be judged relevant or not. Attach the relevance profile and note the asset inventory version it came from.

evidenceHint.en: The relevance profile, listing the technologies intelligence is matched against

title.en: Define how an intelligence item is triaged, rated and routed to an owner

description.en: Write the procedure: how relevance is decided against the profile, the rating scale applied, which team receives which category of item, and how an item that warrants immediate action is escalated. Attach the approved triage procedure.

evidenceHint.en: The approved triage and routing procedure, including the rating scale

title.en: Record every relevant intelligence item, its assessment and the action taken

description.en: For each item that passes triage, log the source, date, what it concerns, the relevance decision and rating, the owner it was routed to, and the action taken or the reason none was needed. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: The threat intelligence log, one row per item with rating, owner and action

title.en: Issue the threat summary to the audiences that act on it

description.en: Produce the consolidated summary for the period covering what was seen, what changed in the threat picture for the organisation's technologies, and what is recommended, and distribute it to the technical and management audiences named in the triage procedure. Attach the issued summary and its distribution list.

evidenceHint.en: The issued threat summary for the period, with its distribution list

title.en: Compare the intelligence received against the incidents and vulnerabilities actually seen

description.en: For the period, check whether the sources warned of what actually occurred, whether items dismissed as irrelevant later mattered, and where a source produced nothing usable; record the coverage gaps and the resulting changes to the source list. Attach the coverage assessment.

evidenceHint.en: The coverage assessment, with source gaps and the changes made to the source list

title.en: State which projects must involve information security and where the test is applied

description.en: Write the criteria that bring a project into scope — it introduces or changes a system, handles a kind of information the organisation has not handled before, opens a new external exposure, brings in a new third party, or changes an existing control — and name the point in the organisation's project method at which every project is tested against them. Attach the criteria and the step in the method that references them.

evidenceHint.en: In-scope criteria plus the named step in the project method where they are applied

title.en: Name the security work an in-scope project must do, when in its life each item falls due, and who decides it is done

description.en: List the security work an in-scope project has to carry out — the assessment done at the outset, the work its results call for, what must be settled before the project's output is put to real use, and what must be settled before the project is closed. Against each item record the point in the project's life at which it falls due, expressed in whatever terms the organisation actually uses to run work — a stage the method names, a checkpoint, a decision to proceed, or the state the work has reached — and the role that decides the item has been done. Where projects are delivered inside a method the organisation does not control, record how each item is placed within that method and who takes the decision there. Attach the schedule of security work with its due point and its deciding role against every item.

evidenceHint.en: Schedule of the security work required of an in-scope project, each item with the point in the project's life at which it falls due and the role that decides it is done

title.en: Produce the security questions a project answers when it comes into scope

description.en: Build the set of questions each in-scope project must answer at initiation: what information it will handle and how sensitive that is, who will need access to it, what it has to stay available for, which third parties are involved, and which obligations apply. Attach the question set as it will be given to projects.

evidenceHint.en: The initiation question set that projects complete on entering scope

title.en: Record the security risks each in-scope project raised, their owners and what was decided

description.en: For every project in scope during the period, produce the record of the risks surfaced by its initiation answers and by its later stages: what the risk is, who owns it, what treatment was decided, and for anything accepted rather than treated, who accepted it. Attach the record for each project.

evidenceHint.en: Per-project risk record with owner, treatment decision, and the named acceptor of every accepted risk

title.en: Record each stage decision and, at close, what passes to the permanent owner

description.en: Capture at every stage the decision taken (proceed, proceed with conditions, hold), the conditions attached to it and who took it; at close, record what transfers to the person who will own the delivered thing — residual risks, conditions still open — and that owner's acceptance of them. Attach the decision record for each in-scope project.

evidenceHint.en: Decision record per project: stage decisions with conditions and approver, and a close entry naming who took on the residual risk

title.en: Sample closed projects and check the security work each stage required was actually done

description.en: Take the projects closed during the period and for each look for the initiation answers, the risk record, a decision at every stage the method names, and a close entry with a named owner for what remained open. Record every miss and how it was put right. Attach the sample review.

evidenceHint.en: Sample review of closed projects listing the missing items per project and their remediation

templates.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets

title.en: Walk each business process and record the information it creates, holds and transmits

description.en: Take each business process or service in turn with the person who runs it and capture the information it handles together with everything that holds that information — systems, databases, shared drives, physical files, and services others run on your behalf. Consolidate what you collect into one inventory. Attach it, with one row per information asset naming its type, where it is held and the process it serves.

evidenceHint.en: Consolidated inventory, one row per asset with its type, where it is held and the process it serves

title.en: Record a named accountable owner against every inventory entry

description.en: For each row identify the individual accountable for that asset being protected and record their name and role. Where a row has no natural owner, put it to management for a decision and record the outcome rather than leaving the field empty. Attach an inventory export showing the owner column with no blanks, plus the decision record for any asset whose ownership was disputed.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory export with every owner field populated, plus the decision record for disputed assets

title.en: Write down what every inventory entry must carry before it is accepted

description.en: State the mandatory fields for a record — identifier, asset type, owner, where it is held, the process or service it supports — the permitted values for each, and who may create or amend an entry. This is what stops the inventory decaying into free text as entries accumulate. Attach the record specification.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory record specification listing every mandatory field, its permitted values, and who may create or amend a record

title.en: Add, amend and retire entries as assets arrive, move and go out of use

description.en: Run the inventory as a live register: enter new assets when a system goes live or a data set is acquired, amend entries when the owner or the holding location changes, and mark retired assets with the date they went out of use rather than deleting the row. Attach the change history for the period showing every addition, amendment and retirement with its date and the person who made it.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory change history for the period: each addition, amendment and retirement with its date and the person who made it

title.en: Reconcile the information asset inventory against an independent source of what exists

description.en: Choose a source built independently of the inventory — the records the teams running the systems keep for themselves, the services actually being paid for, the contracts held with third parties — and compare it against the inventory line by line. List what exists but is not recorded, and what is recorded but no longer exists, and drive each item to a resolution. Attach the reconciliation naming the source used, both discrepancy lists, and the action taken on every item.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation naming the independent source, both discrepancy lists, and the resolution of each item

templates.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
templates.description: Define acceptable use rules for assets

title.en: List the asset classes the acceptable-use rules must cover, and who handles each

description.en: Take the information asset inventory and derive from it the distinct classes of thing a person handles unaided — computers and mobile devices, removable media, email and messaging, collaboration and file-sharing services, printed output, network access — and record against each the population that handles it. This list is the table of contents for the rules. Attach it.

evidenceHint.en: Asset-class list with the user population recorded against each class

title.en: State what a user may do, may not do, and may do only with permission, for each class

description.en: For every class on the list write, in language a user can act on, what is permitted, what is forbidden, and what is allowed only with permission obtained first — covering personal use, moving organisational information onto personal accounts or personal devices, and use of services the organisation has not approved. Attach the rules with a named section per asset class.

evidenceHint.en: Acceptable use rules with a section per asset class stating permitted, forbidden and conditional uses

title.en: Name who grants the permissions the rules make conditional, and how a user asks

description.en: For each conditional use in the rules record who is entitled to grant it, what they need to establish before granting it, how long a grant lasts, and the route by which a user asks for one. Attach the authorisation table alongside the rules.

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation table naming the grantor, the basis for granting and the duration for every conditional use

title.en: Record each person's acknowledgement when they are first given assets, and issue the current rules whenever they change

description.en: When a person is first given any asset on the list, put the current rules in front of them and record their acknowledgement, covering contractors and third-party account holders as well as employees, and chase the people who have not responded rather than closing the round with gaps. When the rules are revised, issue the new version to everyone they bind and record that it went out and to whom. Decide for each revision, and write down the reason, whether the change is substantial enough to warrant collecting acknowledgements again — a fresh round is a judgement about that change, not something every amendment owes. Attach the acknowledgement record for people newly given assets, the issue record for each revision, and the list of responses still outstanding.

evidenceHint.en: Acknowledgement record naming person, rules version and date, the issue record for each revision, and the outstanding-response list

title.en: Classify the misuse reported in the period as a rule broken or a rule unclear, and amend accordingly

description.en: Collect what was reported during the period as misuse of an asset and decide for each case whether the rule was clear and was broken, or whether it did not say plainly enough what to do. Amend the wording where the second applies; repeated cases against one clause are a defect in the rules, not only in the person. Attach the record with each case classified and the resulting amendment or the explicit decision to leave the wording alone.

evidenceHint.en: Record of reported misuse for the period, each case classified, with the resulting amendment or no-change decision

templates.title: Return of assets
templates.description: Ensure return of assets upon termination

title.en: Build a register of the assets issued to each person, keyed to the holder

description.en: Pull issued laptops, phones, tokens, keys, access cards, removable media, licensed software and physical documents from asset management, procurement and facilities records, and key every item to the individual holding it. Assets nobody can be shown to hold are the ones that never come back. Evidence: the issued-asset register with one row per item, naming the holder, the issue date and the issuing function.

evidenceHint.en: Issued-asset register keyed to holder, with issue date and issuing function per item

title.en: Add an asset-return step to the leaver and role-change checklists

description.en: Amend the offboarding and internal-transfer checklists so that the issued-asset register is queried for the individual and each item is explicitly cleared, with the step held open until every line is closed. Name the function responsible for clearing each asset type. Evidence: the amended checklists showing the return step, the register query it depends on and the sign-off it requires.

evidenceHint.en: The amended leaver and role-change checklists showing the asset-return step and its sign-off

title.en: Sign off each departure's asset return against the issued-asset register

description.en: At each departure or role change, work the individual's register rows and record for each item whether it was returned, its condition and the date, closing the row on return. Where an item is not returned, record it as outstanding rather than closing the checklist. Evidence: the completed return records per departure, naming the holder, each item and its return or outstanding status.

evidenceHint.en: Completed asset-return records per departure, itemised with return date or outstanding status

title.en: Record the removal of organisational information from assets that cannot be physically returned

description.en: Where a leaver used a personally owned device, a personal cloud account or remote infrastructure the organisation cannot repossess, run the removal or remote wipe and capture the confirmation. Note the information that was held and the method used. Evidence: the wipe or removal confirmations per departure, naming the device or account, the information affected and the date of removal.

evidenceHint.en: Remote wipe or removal confirmations naming the device or account, the information held and the removal date

title.en: Reconcile outstanding register rows against the departures recorded in the period

description.en: List every departure and role change in the period, pull the register rows still open against those individuals, and drive each to recovery, replacement or a written write-off. Report items still outstanding at the end rather than closing the reconciliation. Evidence: the reconciliation showing every departure, its open items and the recovery, write-off or still-outstanding status of each.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of departures against open register rows, with recovery, write-off or outstanding status per item

title.en: Define the classification levels and the criteria that place information in each

description.en: Agree a small set of levels and write, for each, the test a person applies to decide whether information belongs there — the harm from disclosure, from corruption and from unavailability. Include worked examples of real organisational information at each level so the test can be applied without interpretation. Evidence: the classification scheme, one section per level with its criteria and at least one worked example.

evidenceHint.en: The classification scheme with criteria and worked examples for each level

title.en: Record the minimum classification each legal, contractual or regulatory obligation demands

description.en: Work through data protection obligations, customer contract clauses, sector regulation and confidentiality undertakings, and record for each the categories of information it covers and the minimum level that information must therefore carry. This is what makes classification follow business need rather than preference. Evidence: the obligations table mapping each source obligation to the information categories it covers and the minimum level it forces.

evidenceHint.en: Obligations table mapping each legal or contractual source to the information covered and the minimum level required

title.en: Assign a classification level to every information asset already in the inventory

description.en: Work the asset inventory row by row with each asset's owner, apply the criteria and the obligations table, and record the resulting level against the entry. Record the reasoning for any asset where the owner and the criteria disagreed. Evidence: the inventory export showing a populated classification for every entry, plus the notes on contested assignments.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory export with a classification level on every entry, plus notes on contested assignments

title.en: Classify newly created and newly acquired information as it enters the inventory

description.en: Make classification part of accepting a new information asset: no entry is completed without a level, applied by the asset owner using the published criteria. Cover data sets acquired from customers and third parties as well as internally created information. Evidence: the inventory additions for the period, each showing the level assigned, by whom and on what date.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory additions for the period, each with the level assigned, the assigner and the date

title.en: Re-check the classification of assets whose sensitivity or value has changed

description.en: Identify assets affected by a change in use, a new contractual obligation, aggregation with other data, or the passage of time that reduces sensitivity, and re-apply the criteria to each. Record both upward and downward reclassifications, since over-classification carries its own cost. Evidence: the reclassification record listing each asset, its previous and new level, and the change that triggered the re-check.

evidenceHint.en: Reclassification record with previous level, new level and triggering change per asset

templates.title: Labelling of information
templates.description: Implement labelling procedures for classified information

title.en: List the forms classified information takes and the point at which each can be marked

description.en: Work with the functions that produce and hold information and enumerate the concrete forms it exists in — documents and spreadsheets, messages, extracts drawn from structured data, removable media, printed output, information shown on screens, and physical files. For each form record the producing function and the point in its life at which a marking can be attached without altering the information itself. Attach the form list, one row per form with its producing function and its marking point.

evidenceHint.en: Form list naming each form classified information takes, its producing function and the point at which it can be marked

title.en: Set out the marking that stands for each classification level in each form

description.en: For every level in the classification scheme and every form on the list, write down the exact wording of the marking, where on the item it appears, and what it must survive — copying, printing, extraction, and conversion into another form. Include what a person does when a form cannot carry a visible marking at all. Attach the labelling procedure containing a level-by-form table.

evidenceHint.en: Labelling procedure with a level-by-form table giving the exact marking wording and its placement

title.en: Record who applies the marking for each form and what stands in where none can be carried

description.en: Take each form on the list and record whether the marking is put on by the person producing the information, by the process that produces it, or by a controlling function at the point of issue, and name the accountable role in each case. Where a form genuinely cannot carry a marking, record the substitute that ties the item to its level — an accompanying note, a register entry, a marked container. Attach the application map covering every form on the list, with none left unassigned.

evidenceHint.en: Application map naming the accountable role per form and the substitute recorded for forms that cannot carry a marking

title.en: Apply the marking, or the recorded substitute, as classified information is produced and as it is received

description.en: Apply the defined marking at the moment information is created, extracted or printed. Where the form cannot carry a marking at all, apply instead the substitute recorded against that form in the application map — the accompanying note, the register entry, the marked container. Information arriving from third parties is brought to the level it warrants under the local scheme rather than leaving another organisation's marking to be read as though it were local. Attach a sample of items from the period covering each form on the list, each item showing either the marking the procedure specifies for that form and level or the substitute recorded against that form, and including items received from third parties.

evidenceHint.en: Sample of items from the period covering each form on the list, each showing its specified marking or the recorded substitute, including items received from third parties

title.en: Change the marking on information whose classification level has moved

description.en: When an asset's classification changes, locate the copies and forms already in circulation, apply the new marking or withdraw the item, and record what was reached and what could not be. Downward changes matter as much as upward ones, since a marking left too high keeps information from people who are entitled to it. Attach the re-marking record naming the asset, its old and new level, and the items changed, withdrawn or found unreachable.

evidenceHint.en: Re-marking record per reclassified asset naming old and new level and the items changed, withdrawn or unreachable

title.en: Sample held information and record where the marking does not match its classification

description.en: Draw a sample across the forms on the list, compare the marking on each item against the level its asset carries, and record every mismatch — unmarked, marked too low and marked too high alike. Correct the sampled items and note where repeated errors point at a form whose marking point does not work in practice. Attach the sampling record with expected marking, actual marking and the correction applied for each item.

evidenceHint.en: Sampling record listing each item's expected and actual marking, the mismatches found and the corrections applied

templates.title: Information transfer
templates.description: Secure information transfer policies and procedures

title.en: List the routes information travels on to leave a team or the organisation

description.en: Enumerate every route in use — messaging, file exchange, portals and interfaces run by the organisation or by the other party, physical carriage of media and paper, and spoken exchange in meetings and calls — and include routes that cross an internal boundary where the receiving part of the organisation is governed separately. Record the direction, the kinds of information typically carried, and a named owner for each route. Attach the route list.

evidenceHint.en: Transfer route list with direction, the information typically carried and a named owner per route

title.en: State for each classification level which routes may carry it and what must be true before it is sent

description.en: Produce the rule table: for every level, the routes that may carry it, the routes that may not, the protection the information must have against interception, alteration and delivery to the wrong party, and how the sender confirms the recipient is the intended one and is entitled to receive. Say what a sender is to do when the permitted route is unavailable. Attach the table with one row per classification level.

evidenceHint.en: Transfer rules table showing permitted routes, prohibited routes, required protection and recipient confirmation per level

title.en: Set out what sender and receiver are each responsible for on a transfer, and what is done when one goes astray

description.en: For the routes on the list, write down who is responsible for what when information travels. On the sending side: who may send information at each level by that route, what they must do to carry out the rule for that route and level, and how they establish that it arrived rather than assuming it did. On the receiving side: what the receiving party is expected to do for the transfer to be complete — acknowledge receipt, check the information arrived intact and readable, or say that it did not. Then record what is done when a transfer miscarries: sent to the wrong party, delivered to nobody, or found afterwards to have gone without the protection the rule required. Say what is attempted to retrieve, recall or render useless what was sent, who is told, and by which route it is raised as a security event, without restating the event process here. Attach the responsibilities statement covering every route on the list together with the miscarriage steps.

evidenceHint.en: Statement of sender and receiver responsibilities for every route on the list, plus the steps taken when a transfer miscarries

title.en: Record the transfers of the most sensitive information made in the period

description.en: For the levels the rules single out as most sensitive, keep a record of each transfer outside the organisation: what was sent, to whom, on which route, by whom, on what date, and which protection was applied — using whatever record the route itself produces and a written entry where it produces none. Attach the transfer record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Transfer record for the period naming content, recipient, route, sender, date and the protection applied

title.en: Check that each route delivers the protection its rule requires

description.en: Take the routes one at a time and establish by observation rather than assumption that the stated protection is actually in force — inspect a completed transfer end to end, have the route's owner demonstrate the protection, and where it is safe to do so attempt a transfer the rules prohibit and record whether it was prevented or noticed. Attach the check record naming, per route, what was done, what was observed and whether it met the rule.

evidenceHint.en: Per-route check record stating what was tested, what was observed and the pass or fail against the rule

templates.title: Access control
templates.description: Establish access control policy and rules

title.en: List the systems and information stores the access rules must cover

description.en: Enumerate the applications, infrastructure, data stores, shared repositories, externally hosted services and administrative consoles that hold or reach organisational information, and record for each a named owner, the information it holds and the highest classification that information carries. Attach the scope list; a system absent from it is one no rule will ever be written for.

evidenceHint.en: Scope list naming each in-scope system, its owner, the information it holds and its highest classification

title.en: Write the access rule for each system, naming the roles and the level of access each may hold

description.en: For every system on the scope list, state which job roles may hold read, contribute and administrative access, what business need must exist before each is given, and which combinations one person must not hold — carrying across the conflicting duty pairs already agreed rather than restating them. Set the strictness from the classification recorded against the system rather than from custom. Attach the access control rules, one rule per system on the list.

evidenceHint.en: Access control rules with one rule per in-scope system naming eligible roles, access levels and forbidden combinations

title.en: Record the default stance and the conditions for access no rule covers

description.en: Decide and write down, per system, whether access is refused unless a rule permits it or allowed unless a rule forbids it, and record who may authorise access that no rule covers, what must be true for that to happen, and how long such access may stand before it is revisited. Attach the recorded stance per system together with the standing list of access held outside the rules and the authorisation behind each entry.

evidenceHint.en: Recorded default stance per system plus the standing list of access held outside the rules with its authorisation

title.en: Write the access rule for each system brought into use before anyone is given access to it

description.en: As each new system, data store or externally hosted service enters service, add it to the scope list with its owner and classification and record the rule that governs access to it; where no existing rule fits, record the decision taken and who took it rather than leaving the system unruled. Attach the rule entries added in the period, each naming the system, the date it entered service and the date its rule was recorded.

evidenceHint.en: Rule entries added in the period naming the system, its date of entry to service and the date its rule was recorded

title.en: Re-test each rule against current business need and cover the systems no rule reaches

description.en: Walk the rules with each system owner and confirm that the roles named still exist, still need that access, and still match the classification of the information held, amending the rules that no longer fit and recording those confirmed unchanged. In the same pass, compare the systems actually in use against the scope list and write a rule for anything found uncovered. Attach the review record with a confirm, amend or newly written outcome for every system.

evidenceHint.en: Rule review record with a confirm, amend or newly written outcome per system, including systems found uncovered

templates.title: Identity management
templates.description: Manage identity lifecycle for access control

title.en: List the identity types in use and the directories that hold each

description.en: Enumerate the categories of identity the organisation issues — employee, contractor, temporary, third-party, customer, service and shared identities — and record which directory, application account store or cloud tenancy holds each category. Identities held outside the central directory are the ones that survive a leaver process. Evidence: the identity register naming each identity type, its holding directory and the population size.

evidenceHint.en: Identity register naming each identity type, its holding directory and its population size

title.en: Define the lifecycle events that create, change and disable an identity, and the trigger for each

description.en: Write the procedure connecting a real-world event to an identity action: hire, contract start, internal transfer, extended absence, contract end and departure, and for each name the authoritative source that signals it and the identity action it forces. Cover contractor and third-party identities, which usually have a different signalling source from employees. Evidence: the identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its authoritative trigger and the resulting create, amend or disable action.

evidenceHint.en: Identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its authoritative trigger and identity action

title.en: Record the justification and named human owner for every shared and service identity

description.en: Work through the shared accounts, service accounts and machine identities found in the register; for each, record why an individual identity could not be used, the human accountable for it, the systems it reaches and how its credential is held. Where no justification survives contact, schedule the identity for replacement. Evidence: the shared and service identity register, one row per identity with its justification, its named owner and its credential custody arrangement.

evidenceHint.en: Shared and service identity register with justification, named owner and credential custody per identity

title.en: Disable identities on the leaver trigger and record the elapsed time from trigger to disablement

description.en: On each departure or contract end, disable the individual's identities across every directory in the register, and record both the moment the authoritative trigger fired and the moment each identity was disabled. Recording the interval is what makes the delay visible and improvable. Evidence: the leaver identity records for the period, naming the person, each identity disabled, the trigger timestamp and the disablement timestamp.

evidenceHint.en: Leaver identity records naming each identity disabled, with trigger timestamp and disablement timestamp

title.en: Reconcile active identities against the authoritative people, contractor and service records

description.en: Extract the active identities from every directory in the register and match them against the current people record, the contractor schedule and the service identity register. List identities with no matching current holder, dormant identities, and holders with identities in directories their role does not require, and drive each to disablement or a recorded exception. Evidence: the reconciliation output listing orphaned and dormant identities with the disablement or exception decision on each.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation output listing orphaned and dormant identities with the disablement or exception decision per line

templates.title: Authentication information
templates.description: Manage allocation and use of authentication info

title.en: List the kinds of authentication information in use and where each is held

description.en: For every system a person or a process signs in to, record the kinds of authentication information it accepts — secrets the holder chooses, credentials issued to a named holder, and credentials used by systems and scripts with no person behind them — and where each is kept once it has been issued. Attach the register, one row per system and kind, naming the holder population and the place of custody.

evidenceHint.en: Register of authentication information by system and kind, naming the holder population and where the credential is held

title.en: Set out how a request is authorised and the recipient confirmed before authentication information is issued or replaced

description.en: Write the procedure covering first issue and every later replacement, for both kinds of entry on the register. Where the credential has a person behind it: what establishes that the person asking is the holder, how the credential reaches them without passing through anyone else's hands or records, whether it must be replaced by the holder before it can be used for real work, and what is done when a request arrives and the holder cannot be reached in the usual way. Where the credential belongs to a system, service or script with no person behind it: who may request one, what authorises the request, the named role accountable for the credential once it exists, and how it is placed into the system that will use it without being exposed on the way. Attach the issuance and replacement procedure, covering both kinds.

evidenceHint.en: Issuance and replacement procedure covering person-held and system-held credentials: what authorises the request, how the recipient is confirmed, and first use

title.en: State what makes each kind of authentication information strong enough and how long it stays valid

description.en: For each kind on the register, record the requirement — what an acceptable secret or credential must be, whether it may be reused anywhere else, and the point at which it ceases to be valid — and note against each system whether the requirement is upheld by the system itself or depends on the holder observing it, since the second needs a different kind of assurance. Attach the requirement statement together with the per-system note of how it is upheld.

evidenceHint.en: Requirement statement per kind of authentication information, with a per-system note of how it is upheld

title.en: Record each issue, replacement and withdrawal of authentication information with the confirmation performed

description.en: Every time authentication information is allocated, replaced or withdrawn, record who asked, who carried it out, how the holder was confirmed and the date, writing the entry as the act is done rather than reconstructing it afterwards. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Log of issues, replacements and withdrawals for the period, each naming the requester, the performer and the confirmation made

title.en: Replace authentication information that has been exposed or has outlived its purpose

description.en: When a credential is disclosed in the course of support, turns up somewhere it should not be held, is left over from work that has ended, or is held by someone no longer entitled to it, replace or withdraw it and record what was done. Attach the replacement record naming each credential, the reason it was replaced, the systems affected and the date.

evidenceHint.en: Replacement record naming each credential replaced or withdrawn, the reason, the systems affected and the date

title.en: Establish that credentials supplied with a product or created at installation can no longer be used

description.en: Work the register system by system and establish for each that any credential that arrived with the product or was created when it was installed has been removed or replaced — by demonstrating that it is refused, or from the system's own list of holders. Record the systems where this could not be established as findings rather than as passes. Attach the check record, one row per system with the outcome.

evidenceHint.en: Check record with one row per system stating what was checked and whether a supplied credential remains usable

templates.title: Access rights
templates.description: Provision, review and revoke access rights

title.en: Catalogue the access profiles each system offers and what each one permits

description.en: For every system, list the roles, groups or entitlement sets a person can be given and state in plain words what each one lets the holder see and do, marking those that grant administrative or otherwise unrestricted reach. Attach the entitlement catalogue; without it neither an approver nor a reviewer has anything to judge against.

evidenceHint.en: Entitlement catalogue naming each system, each profile it offers and what that profile permits

title.en: Record who must approve each profile and what the approval has to state

description.en: Map every profile in the catalogue to the person or role whose agreement is needed before anyone holds it, and set out what an approval must contain — the person, the profile, the business reason, and how long it is needed for. State how the approval is captured so that it can be produced later against the grant it authorised. Attach the approval map covering every profile in the catalogue.

evidenceHint.en: Approval map giving the required approver and the required contents of an approval for every catalogued profile

title.en: Grant access only against a recorded approval and keep the approval with the grant

description.en: For each grant made in the period record the person, the system, the profile, the approval relied on and who carried the grant out, and turn away requests that arrive without an approval rather than granting first and papering over it afterwards. Attach the grants made in the period, each tied to the approval that authorised it.

evidenceHint.en: Grants made in the period, each naming the person, the profile, the approval relied on and who executed it

title.en: Withdraw the access a person no longer needs when they change role or leave

description.en: On each move or departure, list the profiles the person holds, decide keep or remove against what their new position requires, and execute the removals — paying particular attention to access that survives their account being closed, such as membership of groups, access to shared repositories and mailboxes, rights on locally held accounts, and access delegated to others on their behalf. A move that only adds is the accumulation this task exists to stop. Attach the records showing profiles held before, the decision on each and the removals executed.

evidenceHint.en: Role-change and departure records showing profiles held before, the keep or remove decision on each and the removals executed

title.en: Put every holder of each non-administrative profile to its system owner for a keep or remove decision

description.en: When the access review falls due, give each system owner the current holders of every profile in their systems that the catalogue does not mark as granting administrative or otherwise unrestricted reach, and require an explicit keep or remove decision against each named person, refusing blanket approvals covering a whole list. The profiles the catalogue does mark are recertified where privileged access rights are managed: take that recertification's result into this review and record that it was taken in, rather than deciding those holders again here. Where a system offers no profile outside the marked ones, record that and the recertification carried in. Return the removals for execution and confirm they were carried out. Attach the completed review showing the reviewer, the decision per holder, the removals executed, and the privileged result carried in.

evidenceHint.en: Completed access review showing the reviewer, a keep or remove decision per holder, the executed removals, and the privileged recertification result carried in

title.en: Account for every right held that no approval or review decision supports

description.en: Take the rights actually held in each system and match them against the approvals recorded and the decisions returned by the last review. List every right with nothing behind it, every administrative profile whose holders were never approved, and every holder whose right outlived the reason it was granted, then drive each line to removal or to an acceptance recorded against a named owner. Attach the comparison with a disposition on every line.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of held rights against approvals and review decisions, with a removal or recorded acceptance on every line

title.en: Compile a register of suppliers that access information or information systems

description.en: List each supplier, the information or system it reaches, how it reaches it (network access, hosted data, on-site presence, staff augmentation) and the internal business owner. Attach the register; suppliers with no access to information are out of scope and should be excluded deliberately, not overlooked.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier register with access route and business owner per supplier

title.en: Classify each registered supplier by the risk its access presents

description.en: Apply a written criterion — sensitivity of information reached, depth of access, dependence of the business on the service — and record the resulting tier against each supplier. Attach the register carrying the tier column plus the criteria used to assign it.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier register with assigned risk tier and the classification criteria

title.en: State the security assurance required before onboarding a supplier in each tier

description.en: For every tier, write down what must be obtained before access is granted — assessment questionnaire, certification or audit report, technical review, contractual commitments. Attach the tiered requirements so an onboarding decision can be checked against a stated bar.

evidenceHint.en: Tiered supplier security requirements document

title.en: Assess each new supplier against its tier's requirements before access is granted

description.en: Run the assurance activity the tier demands, record the findings and any accepted shortfalls, and note who approved granting access. Attach the completed assessment for each supplier onboarded in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Completed pre-onboarding assessment per supplier onboarded in the period

title.en: Reconcile the supplier register against externally held accounts and engaged third parties

description.en: Compare the register with the external identities present in the organisation's systems and with third parties actually engaged by the business, to find suppliers that gained access without being registered. Attach the reconciliation and the disposition of each supplier found outside the register.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing unregistered suppliers found and how each was handled

templates.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
templates.description: Include security requirements in supplier contracts

title.en: Draw up the set of security clauses a supplier agreement must contain

description.en: Derive the clause set from the supplier tiers — confidentiality, permitted use of information, incident notification, subcontracting consent, personnel screening, return or deletion of information on exit, and the right to verify. State which clauses apply to which tier. Attach the clause set.

evidenceHint.en: Required-clause set, mapped to supplier tier

title.en: Insert the required security clauses into the standard supplier contract template

description.en: Amend the organisation's standard agreement and any framework or purchase-order terms so the clause set is the default rather than negotiated case by case. Attach the updated template with the security clauses marked and the version date visible.

evidenceHint.en: Updated contract template with the security clauses marked

title.en: Record which required clauses each active supplier agreement actually contains

description.en: Read every in-force agreement for registered suppliers and mark, clause by clause, whether it is present, absent or weakened by negotiation. Attach the coverage matrix of supplier against clause — this is what turns the template into an assertion about signed contracts.

evidenceHint.en: Clause-coverage matrix, supplier by required clause

title.en: File the executed agreement or amendment for each supplier onboarded in the period

description.en: For every supplier taken on, store the signed agreement (or the signed security amendment to an existing one) against its register entry so the contract is retrievable without asking the business owner. Attach the executed documents filed for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Executed agreements or security amendments filed against register entries

title.en: Resolve each active agreement that is missing a required clause

description.en: Take every gap from the coverage matrix and record the route chosen — renegotiation at renewal, a side letter, a compensating technical or operational measure, or a documented acceptance — together with who decided. Attach the gap list with a disposition against every entry.

evidenceHint.en: Clause-gap list with the decision and decision-maker for each gap

templates.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain

title.en: List the ICT products and services acquired and the supplier behind each

description.en: Cover hardware, purchased and open-source software, cloud components and outsourced development or support. Record the supplier, where the component runs and which business service depends on it. Attach the ICT component list; it is the population every other task here works over.

evidenceHint.en: ICT component list: product or service, supplier, where it runs, dependent service

title.en: Obtain from each ICT supplier the subcontractors and upstream components it relies on

description.en: Ask each supplier on the list to declare its own sub-suppliers, sub-processors and any critical third-party components embedded in what it delivers, and record where a supplier declines or cannot answer. Attach the per-supplier dependency declarations.

evidenceHint.en: Per-supplier dependency declarations, including non-responses

title.en: Set the security acceptance criteria applied before an ICT product or service is adopted

description.en: State what an acquisition must satisfy: provenance and authenticity checks, a secure default configuration, vulnerability disclosure and patching commitments, notification of subcontractor change, and a component inventory where the supplier can provide one. Attach the criteria document.

evidenceHint.en: ICT acquisition security acceptance criteria

title.en: Record the acceptance check performed for each ICT product or service adopted in the period

description.en: For every acquisition, work the criteria, record the evidence the supplier provided against each one, and note the accept, accept-with-conditions or reject decision and who made it. Attach the completed acceptance records.

evidenceHint.en: Completed acceptance record per acquisition with the decision and decision-maker

title.en: Verify the authenticity and integrity of delivered software and firmware before deployment

description.en: Check the supplier's signature or published checksum against what was received, from a source independent of the download itself, and record the result before the artefact reaches a production system. Attach the verification records for releases deployed in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Signature or checksum verification records per release deployed

title.en: Review the ICT component list for entries that no longer meet the acceptance criteria

description.en: Check each entry for end of vendor support, unresolved disclosed vulnerabilities, and notified changes of subcontractor or ownership. Record the action taken for each entry that fails — replace, upgrade, isolate, or formally accept. Attach the review with a per-entry outcome.

evidenceHint.en: ICT component review with the outcome recorded against every entry

templates.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services

title.en: Record what each supplier owes by way of service and security reporting

description.en: Per supplier, list the reports, attestations, certification renewals and performance figures due, the frequency of each and the internal recipient. Attach the monitoring schedule; a supplier owing nothing should say so explicitly rather than be absent.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier monitoring schedule: report due, frequency, recipient

title.en: Define how a supplier-notified change to its service is assessed before it takes effect

description.en: Write down the route a change notification arrives by, who assesses its security impact, what makes a change material, and how acceptance or objection is recorded and returned to the supplier. Attach the supplier change procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier service change assessment procedure

title.en: Collect and review each supplier report that fell due in the period

description.en: Chase what did not arrive, read what did, and record the reviewer's conclusion plus any finding raised with the supplier. Attach the received reports with review notes; a missing report is itself a finding and should appear as one.

evidenceHint.en: Received supplier reports for the period with review notes and findings raised

title.en: Log every supplier-notified service change and the impact assessment made on it

description.en: Record each notified change, the date it was received and takes effect, the assessor, the security impact found and the response given. Attach the supplier change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier change log with assessment outcome per change

title.en: Hold the periodic service review with each supplier above the risk threshold

description.en: Cover open findings, incidents affecting the service, changes made since the last review, and delivery against agreed levels. Record the actions agreed, their owners and the target dates. Attach the review record per supplier reviewed.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier service review record with agreed actions and owners

templates.title: Information security for use of cloud services

title.en: Compile an inventory of cloud services in use and the information held in each

description.en: Record every SaaS, PaaS and IaaS service, its business owner, the classification of the data held, and the region the data sits in. Attach the cloud inventory; include services paid for by individual teams, not only those procured centrally.

evidenceHint.en: Cloud service inventory: service, owner, data classification, region

title.en: Record the split of security responsibility between the organisation and each cloud provider

description.en: For every inventoried service, state which controls the provider operates and which the organisation must configure or run itself — identity, logging, encryption, backup, patching. Attach the responsibility matrix per service; the organisation's column is the work the remaining tasks act on.

evidenceHint.en: Shared-responsibility matrix per cloud service

title.en: Set the configuration baseline the organisation must apply inside each cloud service

description.en: Cover the customer-side settings the responsibility matrix assigns to the organisation: authentication and MFA, administrative roles, audit logging and its retention, encryption options, and network or public exposure. Attach the baseline for each service.

evidenceHint.en: Customer-side configuration baseline per cloud service

title.en: Write the exit plan for each cloud service holding business information

description.en: State how the information is extracted, in what format, how long extraction takes, and how the provider's copies and backups are deleted on termination. Attach the exit plan per service so a provider change is not blocked by an unanswerable data question.

evidenceHint.en: Cloud exit plan per service, covering extraction and provider-side deletion

title.en: Check each cloud service against its configuration baseline and record deviations

description.en: Run the check on the live tenant rather than from documentation, list every setting that differs from the baseline, and record whether it was corrected or accepted and by whom. Attach the check output per service.

evidenceHint.en: Baseline check output per cloud service with deviations and dispositions

title.en: Search for cloud services adopted outside the approval route and add them to the inventory

description.en: Compare the inventory against sign-ins recorded by the identity provider and against expenditure on cloud vendors, to surface services the inventory does not know about. Attach the review listing each service found and whether it was adopted, migrated or shut down.

evidenceHint.en: Unapproved-cloud review listing services found and their disposition

templates.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation

title.en: Define what counts as an information security incident and set the severity levels

description.en: Write the categories the organisation will use and a severity scale with a worked example at each level, so someone triaging at 2am can classify without a debate. Attach the classification scheme; escalation and response commitments hang off these levels.

evidenceHint.en: Incident classification scheme with categories, severity levels and examples

title.en: Name the incident response roles and the people who hold them

description.en: Define coordinator, technical lead, communications and the authority who may escalate or declare a major incident, and record the named holder and deputy for each, with an out-of-hours contact route. Attach the role sheet with names against roles, not just role titles.

evidenceHint.en: Incident response role assignment sheet with named holders, deputies and contact routes

title.en: Write the incident handling procedure from detection through to closure

description.en: Set out logging, triage against the severity scale, containment, preservation of evidence, escalation and communication, recovery and closure — with the responsible role named at each step. Attach the procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Incident handling procedure covering detection through closure

title.en: Prepare the incident record template that captures timeline, actions and evidence

description.en: Build the form responders will fill in during an incident: detection time and source, classification, actions with timestamps, evidence collected and where it is held, decisions taken and the closure rationale. Attach the template so the record is not improvised mid-incident.

evidenceHint.en: Incident record template with the required fields

title.en: Run an exercise of the incident procedure and record what it exposed

description.en: Take a realistic scenario through the procedure with the named role-holders, timing each step, and record where the plan was unclear, contacts were unreachable or a step could not be performed. Attach the exercise record with the gaps listed.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise record with scenario, participants, timings and gaps identified

title.en: Review closed incidents for procedure steps that did not work as written

description.en: For every incident closed in the period, note where responders departed from the procedure or found it silent, and record the amendment made to the plan, roles or template as a result. Attach the review with a finding and an outcome against each incident.

evidenceHint.en: Post-incident review with per-incident findings and the resulting plan amendments

templates.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
templates.description: Assess and decide on security events

title.en: Define the severity tiers and the conditions that qualify an event as an incident

description.en: Write the classification scheme: for each severity tier, state the observable conditions (data exposure, service loss, unauthorised access) that place an event in it, and state the threshold at which an event is declared an incident rather than closed. Attach the criteria document.

evidenceHint.en: Classification criteria document listing each tier, its observable conditions, and the declaration threshold

title.en: Create the assessment record that captures classification, rationale and decision

description.en: Build the record (form or ticket template) an assessor completes for a reported event, with mandatory fields for the tier assigned, the reasoning against the criteria, and the outcome (declared / closed / referred). Attach the blank template and one completed worked example.

evidenceHint.en: Blank assessment template plus one completed example record

title.en: Route reported events into one queue where each carries a classification field

description.en: Wire the reporting channels (helpdesk, monitoring alerts, staff reports) into a single queue so no event is assessed outside the process, and make the classification field mandatory before an item can be closed. Attach the queue configuration and a screenshot showing the required field.

evidenceHint.en: Queue configuration export showing the intake sources and the mandatory classification field

title.en: Record the tier assigned and the reasoning for every reported event

description.en: For each event that arrives in the queue during the period, complete the assessment record: assign a tier against the published criteria, write the reasoning, and log the decision. Events closed without declaration need the same record as those escalated.

evidenceHint.en: Event log for the period showing one classification, rationale and decision per event

title.en: Re-assess a sample of closed events against the criteria

description.en: Take a sample of events closed during the period, apply the criteria independently, and compare the result with the tier originally assigned. Record every disagreement and whether the original decision was corrected or the criteria clarified.

evidenceHint.en: Sample re-assessment noting sample size, disagreements found, and the correction made for each

templates.title: Response to information security incidents
templates.description: Respond to incidents per documented procedures

title.en: Document the containment, eradication and recovery steps for each incident category

description.en: For each category the classification scheme produces (malware, account compromise, data exposure, service disruption), write the ordered actions a responder takes, the systems and access needed, and the point at which the incident may be closed. Attach the procedure set.

evidenceHint.en: Response procedure covering each incident category with its ordered response steps

title.en: Name the responders and the escalation contact for each severity tier
