description.en: Record who responds at each tier, who they escalate to, and how each is reached out of hours. Confirm each named person has the access the procedure assumes, and attach the contact list with the date each entry was confirmed.

evidenceHint.en: Responder and escalation contact list, dated, with the access confirmation per named responder

title.en: Record the actions, timestamps and decisions taken for each declared incident

description.en: Maintain a running timeline per declared incident: what was observed, what action was taken, by whom, at what time, and the decisions made at each escalation point. The timeline is written during the response, not reconstructed afterwards.

evidenceHint.en: Incident timeline per declared incident, with actor and timestamp on each entry

title.en: Notify the internal and external parties the procedure names for each incident

description.en: For each declared incident, work through the notification list in the procedure — management, affected business owners, customers, regulators or contractual counterparties as applicable — and log who was told, when, and through which channel. Where a party was assessed as not requiring notification, record that assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Notification log per incident showing recipient, channel, timestamp, and the reasoning where no notification was sent

title.en: Run a tabletop exercise of one incident category and record where the procedure failed

description.en: Walk a realistic scenario through the documented steps with the named responders, and capture every point where a step was missing, ambiguous, pointed at a system nobody could reach, or named a person who has left. Raise a correction to the procedure for each.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise report listing the gaps found and the procedure amendment raised for each

templates.title: Learning from information security incidents
templates.description: Learn from incidents to improve security

title.en: Create the post-incident review format capturing cause and contributing factors

description.en: Define the questions a review must answer: what allowed the incident to occur, what allowed it to continue undetected, what worked in the response, and what changes would reduce recurrence or impact. Attach the format and the threshold of incidents it applies to.

evidenceHint.en: Post-incident review template plus the written threshold stating which incidents require one

title.en: Hold a post-incident review for each incident above the review threshold

description.en: Convene the responders and the affected system owners after closure, work through the review format, and record the causes and contributing factors agreed. A review is complete when the record names causes, not just a narrative of events.

evidenceHint.en: Completed review record per qualifying incident, naming causes and contributing factors

title.en: Raise a tracked improvement action for each cause a review identifies

description.en: Convert every cause recorded in a review into an action with a named owner and a target, entered in the tracker rather than left in the review document. Link each action back to the incident it came from so closure can be traced.

evidenceHint.en: Action register entries linked to their source incident, each with owner and status

title.en: Analyse incident causes across the period for repeat occurrences

description.en: Group the period's incidents by cause and category to find causes that recurred, and state for each repeat whether the earlier improvement action was absent, incomplete, or ineffective. Propose the control change indicated.

evidenceHint.en: Trend analysis naming repeat causes, their incident counts, and the control change proposed for each

title.en: Confirm the improvement actions from earlier reviews were implemented

description.en: Take the actions raised from prior post-incident reviews and check the change actually landed in the system, procedure or configuration named — not merely that the ticket was closed. Record any action closed without the change taking effect.

evidenceHint.en: Verification listing each action, the change observed in the target system, and any closed-but-unimplemented actions

templates.title: Collection of evidence
templates.description: Collect and preserve evidence for incidents

title.en: Document how each evidence type is identified, acquired and preserved

description.en: For each type the organisation would need to collect (disk images, memory captures, log exports, cloud audit trails, physical media), record the acquisition method, the tooling used, and how the copy is preserved so it stays usable. Attach the procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Evidence-handling procedure with an acquisition and preservation method per evidence type

title.en: Create the chain-of-custody record used for every collected item

description.en: Build the record that travels with an item: unique identifier, what it is, who collected it, when and from where, and a row for each subsequent transfer of custody. Attach the blank record and one completed example.

evidenceHint.en: Blank chain-of-custody record plus one completed example

title.en: Record custody for each evidence item from collection through to release

description.en: Complete a custody record at the moment each item is collected and add a row at every handover, including transfers to external parties. An item with a gap in its custody chain is recorded as such rather than back-filled.

evidenceHint.en: Custody records for the period's collected items, each showing handler, time and transfer history

title.en: Store each acquired item in the designated repository with an integrity hash

description.en: On acquisition, compute a hash of the item, record it against the item identifier, and place the item in the controlled repository with access restricted to the handling team. Attach the repository listing showing item, hash and acquisition date.

evidenceHint.en: Repository listing with item identifier, hash and acquisition date, plus the repository access list

title.en: Re-verify stored evidence against its recorded hash

description.en: Recompute the hash of each item held in the repository and compare it with the value recorded at acquisition. Report every mismatch or missing item, and record what happened to it.

evidenceHint.en: Verification run output listing item, expected hash, observed hash, and the disposition of each mismatch

title.en: Identify the security controls bypassed or weakened in each continuity mode

description.en: Walk each continuity and failover arrangement (alternate site, degraded mode, manual workaround, emergency access) and list the controls that stop applying or apply more weakly there — authentication, logging, segregation, monitoring. Attach the resulting list keyed by mode.

evidenceHint.en: List of continuity modes, each with the controls that degrade or are bypassed in it

title.en: Record the minimum security requirements that must hold while operating in fallback

description.en: For each continuity mode, state which of the degraded controls must nevertheless be maintained and to what level, and which relaxations are accepted for the duration of a disruption. Attach the requirements statement with the acceptance for each relaxation.

evidenceHint.en: Minimum security requirements per continuity mode, with the accepted relaxations recorded

title.en: Configure the fallback environment to enforce its access control and logging requirements

description.en: Apply the access restrictions, authentication and log forwarding the requirements demand to the alternate site or degraded-mode systems, so they are in place before a disruption rather than configured during one. Attach the configuration export and the log destination showing events arriving from the fallback environment.

evidenceHint.en: Fallback environment configuration export plus log samples proving events reach the central destination

title.en: Record the authorisation and restoration of every control relaxed during a disruption

description.en: When a control is relaxed or emergency access granted during a disruption, log the control, who authorised it, when it started, and when normal operation was restored. Close the loop by confirming the control is back in force after the event.

evidenceHint.en: Relaxation log with control, authoriser, start time, restore time and the post-event confirmation

title.en: Test a disruption scenario and check the minimum requirements actually held

description.en: Invoke or simulate one continuity mode and observe whether the requirements stated for it were met — was access still restricted, were logs still captured, was segregation preserved. Record each requirement as held or breached, with the remediation for breaches.

evidenceHint.en: Test report comparing each stated minimum requirement to the observed control state, with remediation per breach

title.en: Map each ICT service to the recovery time and recovery point its business process requires

description.en: Take the recovery objectives set for the business processes and trace them down to the ICT services, data stores and third-party dependencies each process relies on, so every service carries a target it inherited rather than one invented for it. Attach the mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Service-to-process mapping showing the recovery time and recovery point target inherited by each ICT service

title.en: Write the recovery runbook for each ICT service, including dependency order

description.en: For each in-scope service, document the steps to restore it: where the backup or standby lives, the order dependencies must come up in, the credentials and access needed, and how restoration is confirmed successful. Attach the runbook set.

evidenceHint.en: Recovery runbook per in-scope service, showing restore steps, dependency order and the success check

title.en: Provision the redundancy and backup arrangements the recovery targets require

description.en: Where the mapped target cannot be met by the current arrangement, put the standby capacity, replication or backup frequency in place that makes it achievable, and record for each service what was provisioned. Attach the configuration evidence per service.

evidenceHint.en: Per-service configuration evidence of the backup, replication or standby arrangement supporting its target

title.en: Exercise the recovery runbook for an ICT service and record the achieved recovery time

description.en: Run the runbook against a real restore into an isolated environment, timing it end to end and checking the restored data against the recovery point target. Record where the runbook was wrong or incomplete and correct it.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise record with start and finish times, achieved recovery time and point against target, and the runbook corrections made

title.en: Reconcile the recovery runbooks against the current ICT architecture

description.en: Compare the services and dependencies named in the runbooks with those actually running, and find services introduced or re-platformed since the runbooks were written that no plan covers. Record each unmatched service and the runbook raised for it.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing services with no runbook, runbooks referencing retired systems, and the action for each

templates.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
templates.description: Identify and comply with legal requirements

title.en: Compile the register of legal, regulatory and contractual security obligations

description.en: Enumerate the obligations that bear on information security for each jurisdiction the organisation operates in and each service it delivers, drawing from statute, sector regulation and customer contracts. Record for each the source instrument and the part of the business it binds. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Obligations register with source instrument, jurisdiction and affected service per entry

title.en: Map each register entry to the controls and system owners that satisfy it

description.en: For every obligation, name the control, process or system that meets it and the owner accountable for that control, so an obligation with no control behind it becomes visible. Attach the mapping and list the entries that currently map to nothing.

evidenceHint.en: Obligation-to-control mapping, with the unmapped obligations listed separately

title.en: Record the monitoring source that signals a change for each obligation

description.en: For each register entry, name where a change would be noticed — regulator publication, counsel briefing, contract renewal, industry body — and who watches it. This is what keeps the register current rather than a point-in-time snapshot.

evidenceHint.en: Register column or annex naming the monitoring source and the watcher for each obligation

title.en: Amend the register when a monitored source reports a changed obligation

description.en: When a monitored source reports a new or amended requirement, update the affected register entries, re-check the control mapping still satisfies the changed wording, and notify the owners whose controls are affected. Keep the change history rather than overwriting.

evidenceHint.en: Register change history showing the date, the source that triggered it, the requirement amended and the owners notified

title.en: Assess each in-scope service against its mapped obligations and record gaps

description.en: Take the services in the register and test whether the mapped controls are actually operating as the obligation requires, rather than merely assigned. Record each obligation as met or gapped, with the remediation and owner for every gap.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance assessment listing obligation, service, met/gapped status and the remediation owner per gap

title.en: Inventory the licensed software and third-party material in use

description.en: List the commercial software, subscriptions, datasets, media and other third-party material the organisation uses, and hold the licence, purchase record or terms of use alongside each entry. Attach the inventory with the source document referenced per row.

evidenceHint.en: Software and third-party material inventory, each row referencing its licence or purchase record

title.en: Record the permitted seats, deployments and redistribution limits for each licence

description.en: Read the terms of each licence held and extract what it actually permits — how many users or installs, which environments, whether the material may be modified or passed to customers — so entitlement can be compared with use. Attach the entitlement summary per licence.

evidenceHint.en: Entitlement summary per licence stating permitted seats, environments and redistribution rights

title.en: Restrict software acquisition and installation to approved sources

description.en: Configure the endpoint and server controls so software arrives through the managed catalogue or approved repositories rather than arbitrary downloads, and route purchase requests through the procurement path that records a licence. Attach the policy configuration and the request route.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint and repository configuration showing the installation restriction, plus the documented acquisition route

title.en: Record the open-source components in each product build with their licence obligations

description.en: Generate a component manifest for the build, resolve the licence of every dependency, and flag those carrying attribution, notice or reciprocal-licensing obligations so they can be honoured in what ships. Attach the manifest and the notice file it produces.

evidenceHint.en: Build component manifest with resolved licence per dependency, and the attribution notice shipped with the release

title.en: Reconcile deployed installations against purchased entitlements

description.en: Count actual installs and active seats per product from the management tooling and compare them against the entitlement summary. Record every over-deployment and whether it was resolved by removing installs or buying additional licences.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation showing installs and seats against entitlement per product, with the resolution of each over-deployment

title.en: Scan managed endpoints for software absent from the licence inventory

description.en: Run a discovery scan across managed devices and servers, subtract what the inventory accounts for, and investigate the remainder — unlicensed installs, personal copies, unapproved tooling. Record the disposition of each item found.

evidenceHint.en: Scan output listing software found but not in the inventory, with the disposition recorded per item

templates.title: Protection of records
templates.description: Protect records per legal and business requirements

title.en: Inventory the record classes held and the retention requirement fixing each one

description.en: List each class of record the organisation holds (contracts, financial records, personnel files, audit trails, incident records), and for each one name the system it lives in, its owner, and the specific legal, regulatory, contractual or business requirement that sets how long it must be kept. Where no requirement exists, say so explicitly rather than leaving the cell blank. Attach the completed inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Records inventory listing record class, holding system, owner and the requirement fixing its retention

title.en: Publish a retention schedule giving a period and a disposal method per record class

description.en: Turn the inventory into a schedule: for every record class state the retention period, the event that starts the clock (creation, contract end, employment end), and how the record is disposed of at the end of it (secure deletion, shredding, cryptographic erasure). Legal/DPO owns the periods; IT Operations confirms each disposal method is achievable in the holding system. Attach the approved schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Retention schedule showing period, retention trigger and disposal method for each record class

title.en: Restrict alteration and deletion of records before their retention period ends

description.en: In each system holding records, configure the controls that stop a record being changed or removed early — immutable or write-once storage, retention locks, or removal of delete rights from routine operator accounts — and record which mechanism protects which record class. Where a system cannot enforce it technically, note the compensating control. Attach the configuration exports and the permission listings.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system configuration export and permission listing showing the protection applied to each record class

title.en: Dispose of records that have passed their retention date and log each disposal

description.en: Run the disposal due under the schedule for this period, using the disposal method named for that record class. Log each disposal with the record class, the volume or identifiers covered, the date, the method used and who authorised it, so that a record absent from the system can later be shown to have been disposed of deliberately rather than lost.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal log for the period, one entry per disposal with class, volume, date, method and authoriser

title.en: Retrieve a sample of long-retention records to prove they are still readable

description.en: Pick a sample of records that must be kept for long periods or that sit on legacy media or in obsolete file formats, retrieve them, and confirm they open and are complete. Where a record can no longer be read, record the migration or format conversion needed. Attach the retrieval results including the records sampled and the outcome for each.

evidenceHint.en: Retrieval test record listing the sampled records, the outcome for each, and any remediation raised

title.en: Reconcile records held in each system against the retention schedule

description.en: Compare what each system actually holds against what the schedule says it should hold, and list two things: records still held past their disposal date, and record classes with fewer records than expected (a sign of premature deletion). Record the resolution for each discrepancy. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation showing overdue and prematurely-deleted records per system, with the resolution of each

title.en: Record every processing activity that handles personally identifiable information

description.en: Enumerate the activities in which the organisation collects, uses, stores or shares PII. For each, record the categories of PII involved, the purpose, the systems and storage locations holding it, and whether the organisation acts as controller or processor. Engineering supplies the system and storage detail. Attach the completed processing record.

evidenceHint.en: Processing record listing each activity with PII categories, purpose, systems and controller/processor role

title.en: Register the privacy obligations applying to each processing activity

description.en: Identify the privacy legislation, regulator guidance and customer contract clauses that bind each processing activity in the jurisdictions where it takes place, and map each obligation to the activities it applies to. This is what later assessments are measured against, so an obligation with no activity mapped to it, or an activity with no obligation, must be explained. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Obligations register mapping each privacy obligation to the processing activities it binds

title.en: Document the safeguard relied on for each cross-border transfer of PII

description.en: For every flow of PII out of the jurisdiction where it was collected — including onward flows to sub-processors and support access from other regions — record the destination, the recipient, and the mechanism relied on to permit the transfer. Where the review finds no cross-border flows, record that conclusion and how it was reached. Attach the transfer register.

evidenceHint.en: Transfer register listing destination, recipient and the safeguard relied on for each cross-border PII flow

title.en: Implement the handling route for requests from individuals about their PII

description.en: Define and stand up the path a request takes from receipt to closure: where requests arrive, how the requester's identity is verified, who searches which systems, and who approves the response. Configure the intake channel and the routing so a request cannot sit unassigned. Attach the procedure and evidence the intake channel is live.

evidenceHint.en: Request-handling procedure plus a screenshot or configuration export showing the live intake and routing

title.en: Log every request received from an individual about their PII and its outcome

description.en: Maintain the log of requests handled in the period: date received, request type, systems searched, action taken, date closed. The log is what shows the route in the previous task is actually being used rather than merely documented, so it should also record requests that were refused and the reason.

evidenceHint.en: Request log for the period, one row per request with receipt date, type, action taken and closure date

title.en: Assess each processing activity against the obligations mapped to it

description.en: Walk the processing record against the obligations register and judge, per activity, whether the obligations mapped to it are being met — checking the PII actually held against the purpose recorded, and the safeguards in place against those the obligations require. Record each gap with an owner and a remediation action. Attach the assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Assessment covering every processing activity, with gaps found, owners assigned and remediation actions

title.en: Define the scope of the independent review and who is eligible to perform it

description.en: Write the terms of reference: which policies, processes, systems and controls the review covers, what evidence the reviewer may request, and the independence criterion the reviewer must satisfy — that they do not manage or operate the area under review. Naming the criterion in advance is what stops the review being staffed with the people who run the controls. Attach the agreed terms of reference.

evidenceHint.en: Terms of reference stating review scope, reviewer access rights and the independence criterion

title.en: Set the review programme, including the events that trigger a review out of cycle

description.en: Record when reviews take place — the planned interval between them and the next scheduled date — and list the changes significant enough to trigger a review before that date, such as a major system migration, a change in regulatory scope, or a serious incident. Attach the approved programme.

evidenceHint.en: Review programme showing the interval, the next scheduled review and the events triggering an out-of-cycle review

title.en: Carry out the independent review and issue a report of the findings

description.en: Have the reviewer named under the independence criterion execute the review across the scope in the terms of reference, examining evidence rather than relying on assertions from control owners. The report should state what was examined, the method used, and each finding with the evidence supporting it. Attach the issued report.

evidenceHint.en: Independent review report stating scope, method examined, and each finding with its supporting evidence

title.en: Present the review report to management and record the decisions taken on it

description.en: Put the report to the management body that owns information security, and minute what was decided for each finding — accepted with a remediation action, accepted as a risk, or disputed with the reason. A report filed without a management decision leaves the findings owned by nobody.

evidenceHint.en: Minutes or management record showing the report was presented and the decision recorded against each finding

title.en: Track each review finding through to verified closure

description.en: Maintain the tracker carrying the findings from the report: owner, agreed action, target date, and the evidence that closed it. A finding is closed only when someone has confirmed the fix, not when the owner says the work is done. Attach the tracker showing the current state of every finding from the latest review.

evidenceHint.en: Findings tracker with owner, action, target date and the closure evidence for each finding

templates.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security

title.en: Map each security policy and standard to the manager whose area is checked against it

description.en: List the policies, rules and standards in force, and against each one name the area of responsibility it applies to and the manager who checks compliance within that area. A policy with no area mapped to it will never be checked, so the gaps this exposes are the point of the exercise. Attach the completed mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Mapping of each policy and standard to its area of responsibility and the responsible manager

title.en: Define what a manager inspects to judge compliance with each policy

description.en: For each policy in the mapping, write down the check: what the manager looks at, how much of it (full population or a stated sample size), and the criterion that separates a pass from a failure. Without a stated criterion, two managers checking the same policy will reach different verdicts and neither result is comparable. Attach the check definitions.

evidenceHint.en: Check definition per policy giving the items inspected, the sample, and the pass criterion

title.en: Automate the compliance checks that can be measured from system data

description.en: For those policy requirements a system can evaluate directly — configuration baselines, patch levels, access rights, encryption settings — build the queries or tooling rules that measure conformance and report exceptions, and record which policy requirement each rule covers. Requirements no rule can cover stay on the manual checks defined above. Attach the rule definitions and their coverage mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Automated rule or query definitions with the mapping showing which policy requirement each one covers

title.en: Record each manager's compliance check result for the period

description.en: Collect the completed checks for the period: area checked, policy checked against, date, what was sampled, and the result. This is the record that shows the checks were performed by the responsible manager rather than assumed, so a check not returned is itself a finding to chase.

evidenceHint.en: Completed compliance check records for the period, one per area and policy, with sample and result

title.en: Raise a nonconformity record for every failed check, with its cause and corrective action

description.en: Where a check fails or an automated rule reports an exception, open a record capturing what did not conform, why it happened, the corrective action agreed, its owner and target date. Closing the individual exception without recording the cause leaves the same failure free to recur next period.

evidenceHint.en: Nonconformity records for the period, each with cause, corrective action, owner and target date

title.en: Compare check coverage against the policy mapping and list what went unchecked

description.en: Take the checks actually recorded this period and set them against the full mapping of policies to areas, then list every policy or area with no check performed and the reason. Coverage is the measure that stops the compliance regime quietly shrinking to the few areas that always report. Attach the coverage comparison.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage comparison naming every policy or area with no check recorded in the period, and the reason

title.en: List the operational activities that require a documented procedure

description.en: Enumerate the activities performed on the information processing facilities — system start-up and shutdown, backup and restore, batch and job scheduling, media handling, patching and deployment, monitoring response — and record for each whether a procedure exists today and where it is held. The list of activities with no procedure is the work queue for the next task. Attach the list.

evidenceHint.en: List of operational activities with the facility or system each covers and whether a procedure exists

title.en: Write a procedure for each listed activity that has none

description.en: Produce the missing procedures. Each one should carry the steps in the order performed, the prerequisites and access needed to start, what to do when a step fails, and who to escalate to — enough for a competent operator who has not performed the activity before to complete it. Attach the drafted procedures.

evidenceHint.en: The drafted procedure documents, covering every activity the list flagged as undocumented

title.en: Publish the procedures where operators can reach them and limit who may edit them

description.en: Put the procedures in a single location the operators who need them can access — including during an outage, where the procedure covers recovery — and restrict edit rights to their owners so the operating instruction cannot be altered by anyone reading it. Attach the repository location and the access and edit permissions on it.

evidenceHint.en: Repository location plus a permissions export showing read access for operators and restricted edit rights

title.en: Update the affected procedure whenever its underlying system or process changes

description.en: When a change lands on a facility covered by a procedure, revise the procedure in the same change and record the new version. The evidence for the period is the version history: it shows procedures moving in step with the systems they describe rather than describing a configuration that has since been replaced.

evidenceHint.en: Procedure version history for the period, showing each revision and the change that prompted it

title.en: Walk each procedure through with the operator who performs the activity

description.en: Sit with the operator and follow the written procedure step by step against how the activity is actually carried out, noting every step that is wrong, missing, out of order, or routinely skipped. Record the discrepancies found and the correction made to the document. Attach the walkthrough records.

evidenceHint.en: Walkthrough record per procedure naming the operator, the discrepancies found and the corrections made

title.en: List the roles requiring background verification and the checks each attracts

description.en: Classify every role, employee and contractor alike, by the sensitivity of the information and systems it reaches, then record which verification types (identity, right to work, employment history, qualifications, criminal record, financial) apply at each sensitivity level. Attach the role-to-check matrix, with the sensitivity rationale for any role attracting checks beyond identity.

evidenceHint.en: Role-to-check matrix listing every role, its sensitivity level and the verification types it attracts

title.en: Record what each jurisdiction permits you to check and how long results may be held

description.en: For every country you hire in, work with Legal to write down which of the checks in the matrix are lawful, what candidate consent is needed, and the retention limit on the result. Attach the per-jurisdiction statement; where a check in the matrix is not permitted somewhere, record the compensating measure used instead.

evidenceHint.en: Per-jurisdiction screening statement covering lawful checks, consent basis and retention limits

title.en: Write the screening procedure, covering agency and contractor staff as well as hires

description.en: Set out who initiates a check, who performs it, what a candidate is told, who adjudicates an adverse result, and at what point in onboarding access may be granted. Include how screening is obtained for people supplied by a third party, whether by supplier attestation or by direct check. Attach the procedure with the named adjudicating role.

evidenceHint.en: Screening procedure naming the initiator, performer, adjudicator and the access-grant point

title.en: Record the completed screening result for every person before their access is granted

description.en: Log each person's screening as it completes: the checks run, the date, the adjudication decision, and any residual condition attached to the hire. Keep the underlying evidence restricted to HR. Attach the screening register for the period, which should reconcile one-to-one with the joiners the same period produced.

evidenceHint.en: Screening register for the period: one row per person with checks run, date and adjudication decision

title.en: Sample joiners from the period and confirm each holds the checks their role requires

description.en: Draw a sample across role sensitivity levels and re-verify, from the register, that the checks the matrix demands for that role were completed before access was granted. Attach the sample test showing the population, the rows selected, each exception, and what was done about it.

evidenceHint.en: Sample test recording the population, the joiners selected, exceptions found and their resolution

templates.title: Terms and conditions of employment
templates.description: Include security responsibilities in employment terms

title.en: List every contract and engagement type through which people reach your information

description.en: Enumerate the paper that binds people to the organisation: employment contracts by country, fixed-term and intern agreements, contractor and agency terms, and any letter of engagement. Record the template owner for each. Attach the list, which becomes the population the security clauses must be inserted into.

evidenceHint.en: List of contract and engagement templates in use, with the owner of each

title.en: Draft the security clauses that employment terms must carry

description.en: With Legal, write the clause set stating the individual's information security obligations: confidentiality, acceptable use of systems and data, handling of classified information, return of assets, the consequences of disregard, and which duties survive the engagement. Attach the approved clause set with a note of the obligation each clause carries.

evidenceHint.en: Approved security clause set with the obligation each clause imposes

title.en: Insert the approved clauses into each contract template on the list

description.en: Work through the template population and place the clauses into each, adapting wording where a jurisdiction or engagement type requires it. Attach the updated templates plus a mapping showing which clause landed in which template, and record any template where a clause was deliberately omitted and why.

evidenceHint.en: Updated templates plus a clause-to-template mapping, including deliberate omissions and their reason

title.en: Record each new starter's signed acceptance of the security terms

description.en: As each person joins, file the signed contract or separate acknowledgement evidencing they accepted the security obligations, and note the version of the clause set they signed. Attach the acceptance record for the period so any starter without one is visible.

evidenceHint.en: Acceptance record for the period: person, engagement type, clause-set version, signature date

title.en: Compare contracts held for existing staff against the current clause set

description.en: Check what people already engaged actually signed against the clause set now approved, and identify who is on superseded terms. Attach the gap list naming the affected people or cohorts, the clauses they lack, and the plan for re-papering or obtaining a supplementary acknowledgement.

evidenceHint.en: Gap list of staff on superseded terms, the missing clauses, and the re-papering plan

templates.title: Information security awareness, education and training

title.en: Split the workforce into audiences and record the security topics each one needs

description.en: Group people by what their work exposes — everyone, those who build or administer systems, those who handle the most sensitive information, those who decide what happens to it — and for each group record the topics it must cover, the depth expected, and how often a topic is repeated. Attach the audience-to-topic map, including the reason each specialised audience was separated out and which topics apply to contractors and temporary staff as well as employees.

evidenceHint.en: Audience-to-topic map with the repeat interval and the reason each audience was separated out

title.en: Name the material that covers each topic and who keeps it current

description.en: Work down the map and attach to every audience-topic pairing a specific piece of material — a session, a written brief, a walkthrough, a purchased course, whatever you actually use — naming its owner and the date it was last checked against your own policies rather than generic advice. Attach the inventory; any pairing with nothing behind it is the gap to close first, and should be listed as such.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory naming the material behind every audience-topic pairing, its owner, and the date last checked against current policy

title.en: Decide what counts as evidence that a person has covered a topic

description.en: Before delivery starts, write down what will be accepted as proof for each topic — an attendance record, a signed acknowledgement, an assessment result, a supervisor's confirmation — and who holds it. This keeps the completion record comparable whether a topic is delivered in a room, at a desk, or in writing, and stops the record depending on the way the topic happened to be delivered. Attach the statement of accepted evidence per topic.

evidenceHint.en: Written statement of the evidence accepted for each topic and who holds it

title.en: Record each delivery of a topic and who received it

description.en: As each topic is delivered, capture the date, the audience it was aimed at, the people who took it, and the evidence held for each, including new joiners covering their induction topics. Attach the completion record for the period, laid out so that a person who has not yet covered a topic their audience requires is visible on the face of it rather than inferred by cross-referencing.

evidenceHint.en: Completion record for the period: person, audience, topic, delivery date and the evidence held

title.en: Pursue the people whose required topics are still outstanding

description.en: Take the outstanding names from the completion record, raise each with the person's manager, and follow it to either completion or a recorded exception carrying a reason and an end date. Attach the outstanding list for the period showing how long each name has been overdue, the escalation made, and the date it closed.

evidenceHint.en: Outstanding list per period with the escalation made and the closure date or recorded exception for each name

title.en: Judge whether the awareness and training programme is changing conduct

description.en: Pick a measure that observes what people do rather than that they attended, and state why it is a fair proxy for the behaviour the programme was meant to produce. Record the result for this period, set against the previous period where there is one and stated as the baseline where there is not. Then say what follows from it: the audience or topic whose material you are changing and what is changing, or a recorded conclusion that the material stands as it is, with the reason for that conclusion. Attach the assessment naming the measure, the result and the conclusion drawn.

evidenceHint.en: Effectiveness assessment naming the measure, the result for the period, and either the material being changed or the recorded conclusion that it stands

templates.title: Disciplinary process
templates.description: Define disciplinary process for policy violations

title.en: Write the disciplinary procedure for information security violations

description.en: Set out the path a confirmed violation takes: who receives the referral, how the person is informed and heard, who decides, what record is kept, and how appeal works. State how the procedure interacts with the general HR disciplinary process rather than duplicating it. Attach the procedure with the deciding role named at each step.

evidenceHint.en: Disciplinary procedure for security violations, naming the deciding role at each step

title.en: Grade the severity of violations and set the sanction range for each grade

description.en: Define the grades a violation can attract and the factors that place it there, such as intent, recurrence, the sensitivity of information involved and actual harm caused, then record the sanction range available at each grade. Attach the grading table, so two similar cases cannot draw wildly different treatment.

evidenceHint.en: Grading table mapping severity factors to grades and the sanction range for each grade

title.en: Define when a security incident is referred into the disciplinary process, and to whom

description.en: Agree with incident handling the conditions under which a case stops being purely technical and becomes a conduct matter, who makes that call, and the named recipient in HR. Attach the referral criteria and the handover route, including how evidence is passed without widening access to it.

evidenceHint.en: Written referral criteria and handover route, naming the role that refers and the HR recipient

title.en: Log each disciplinary referral arising from a security violation and its outcome

description.en: Record every referral as it is raised: the date, the grade applied, the decision, the sanction and the closure date, holding the log under HR confidentiality with access restricted to the deciding roles. Attach the referral log for the period, or a nil return if none arose.

evidenceHint.en: Referral log for the period (or a nil return): one row per case with grade, decision and closure date

title.en: Compare closed cases against the grading table for consistency of sanction

description.en: Review the cases closed in the period against the grades and sanction ranges, looking for like cases treated differently or sanctions falling outside the defined range. Attach the review note with the cases compared, any inconsistency found, and whether the fix is to the table or to how it is being applied.

evidenceHint.en: Consistency review note listing the cases compared and any inconsistency and its resolution

templates.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment

title.en: Write the schedule of responsibilities that survive a departure or a change of role

description.en: Working from the engagement terms and confidentiality agreements already in place, list the obligations that continue to bind a person once they leave or move to a different role, the duration of each, and the instrument each comes from. Attach the schedule, distinguishing the obligations that apply on an internal move from those that apply on departure — they are not the same set, and a mover keeps working for you.

evidenceHint.en: Schedule of surviving responsibilities with duration, source instrument, and whether it bites on departure, on an internal move, or both

title.en: Name the trigger and the responsible person for every way an engagement can end or change

description.en: Cover resignation, the end of a fixed term, dismissal with no notice, retirement, an internal move, and a contractor rolling off. For each, record what starts the process, who holds the conversation about continuing responsibilities, and who obtains the acknowledgement. Attach the procedure, including the variant used when a person leaves the same day and the usual sequence is unavailable.

evidenceHint.en: Procedure naming the trigger and the responsible role for each departure and change type, including the no-notice variant

title.en: Define what a leaver or mover must hand over, and to whom

description.en: Set out what a handover has to establish before the person stops doing the work: the duties they carry, the information and records held only by them, the commitments and relationships someone else will inherit, and the named person taking each on. Attach the handover definition — this is the thing a line manager completes for a specific departure, not a general leaver checklist.

evidenceHint.en: Handover definition listing the duties, information and relationships that must be transferred and named to a successor

title.en: Record each leaver's and mover's acknowledgement of what continues to bind them

description.en: As people leave or change role, put the schedule in front of them in their own terms, capture their acknowledgement, note which version of the schedule they were shown, and file it with the personnel record. Attach the acknowledgement record for the period; it should account for every name on the list of people who left or changed role in that period, with a reason recorded against any name that has none.

evidenceHint.en: Acknowledgement record for the period, accounted line by line against the list of leavers and movers, with a reason for each gap

title.en: Record the completed handover for each departure and internal move

description.en: For each person leaving or moving, complete the handover defined above and record who took on each duty and each item of information, and the date the transfer took effect. Attach the completed handovers for the period, showing explicitly any duty that was left unassigned and who is carrying it in the meantime.

evidenceHint.en: Completed handover records for the period naming the successor for each duty, and any duty left unassigned with its interim holder

title.en: Test a sample of departures and moves for the acknowledgement and the handover

description.en: Draw a sample that spans the departure and change types the period actually produced — resignation, end of a fixed term, dismissal, retirement, an internal move, a contractor rolling off — and record on the face of the test which of those types the period produced none of. For each case drawn, check that the acknowledgement names the responsibilities the schedule requires and that the handover assigned every duty and every item of information to a named person. Attach the sample test with the population, the types it covered, the cases drawn, each exception and how it was closed.

evidenceHint.en: Sample test naming the population, the types the period produced and those it did not, the cases drawn, and each exception and its closure

title.en: Identify every relationship in which a confidentiality agreement is required

description.en: Enumerate the counterparties who reach your information, such as employees, contractors, suppliers and their subcontractors, prospects under evaluation, auditors, and site visitors, and record for each whether a signed agreement is required or is covered by another instrument. Attach the list with the requirement decision and its reason.

evidenceHint.en: List of counterparty types with the confidentiality requirement decision and reason for each

title.en: Record what a confidentiality agreement must contain to be acceptable

description.en: Define the mandatory content: how confidential information is identified, permitted use and permitted recipients, the duration of the obligation, return or destruction on termination, what happens on a breach, and governing law. Attach the required-content standard, so a counterparty's own paper can be assessed against it rather than argued case by case.

evidenceHint.en: Required-content standard listing each mandatory element of an acceptable agreement

title.en: Produce the approved agreement templates for each relationship type

description.en: Draft or adapt the templates covering the relationship types identified, including one-way and mutual forms, and note which template serves which relationship. Attach the approved templates and the mapping, together with the escalation route for a counterparty who insists on their own paper.

evidenceHint.en: Approved template set, the relationship each serves, and the escalation route for third-party paper

title.en: Record the executed agreement for each counterparty before information is shared

description.en: Log every agreement as it is signed: counterparty, template used, whether it was amended, signature date, term and expiry. Where the counterparty's own paper was accepted, note the assessment against the required-content standard. Attach the agreement register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Agreement register: counterparty, template, signature date, term, expiry and any accepted deviation

title.en: Review the register for agreements expiring or missing a signed copy

description.en: Work through the register for agreements past or near expiry, relationships still active with no executed agreement, and rows where no countersigned copy was ever filed. Attach the review output listing each finding, the counterparty affected, and whether the agreement was renewed, chased or the relationship stopped.

evidenceHint.en: Register review output listing expiries, gaps and the action taken on each

title.en: Record which roles may work away from organisational premises, and where from

description.en: Decide role by role whether the work can be done away from your premises, whether that extends to a customer or partner site, shared and public spaces, and other countries, and which information or duties must not leave the premises at all. Attach the authorisation record listing role, approving manager, the permitted locations, and each exclusion with the reason it was excluded.

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation record: role, approving manager, permitted locations, and the information or duties excluded from working away

title.en: Write the rules a person must follow when working away from premises

description.en: State what is expected of the person: what they may work on, how they keep screens, papers, conversations and calls from being seen or overheard, how they store and destroy documents and portable items away from the office, what others sharing the space may and may not be given sight of, and what they do the moment equipment or information goes missing. Attach the rules document.

evidenceHint.en: Remote-working rules covering equipment, surroundings, papers and portable items, shared spaces, and loss

title.en: Record what the organisation supplies for working away, and what the person supplies

description.en: For each permitted location type, write down what the organisation issues or pays for, what the person is expected to provide, and the protection relied on for each — for the equipment used, for the way work reaches your information, and for anything taken off site in physical form. Attach the statement, so that where a person's own equipment or a third party's premises are relied on, that reliance is a recorded decision rather than an assumption.

evidenceHint.en: Statement per location type of what the organisation supplies, what the person supplies, and the protection relied on for each

title.en: Record each person's remote-working authorisation as it is granted

description.en: Log every individual arrangement: the person, their role, the locations approved for them, the approval date and approving manager, and what they were issued to make it possible. Record withdrawals the same way when a role changes or an arrangement ends. Attach the remote-working register as it stood at the end of the period.

evidenceHint.en: Remote-working register: person, role, approved locations, approval date, what was issued, and any withdrawal with its date

title.en: Confirm for the period that what the remote-working rules require is actually in place

description.en: Check the people on the register against the rules — by a declaration from them, by their manager's confirmation, or from records you already hold, whichever you rely on — and record what was confirmed for each and how. Attach the confirmation results for the period naming every shortfall, what was missing, and whether it was corrected or the arrangement withdrawn.

evidenceHint.en: Confirmation results for the period naming each shortfall and whether it was corrected or the arrangement withdrawn

title.en: Reconcile who is working away from premises against the authorisation record

description.en: Compare the register against who is genuinely working away today, looking for arrangements that outlived a role change or a departure, people working from a location their role does not permit, and people working away with no recorded authorisation at all. Attach the reconciliation naming each discrepancy and the withdrawal or fresh authorisation that resolved it.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of the register against current practice, with each discrepancy and the action that resolved it

templates.title: Information security event reporting
templates.description: Enable personnel to report security events

title.en: Write, in the words staff use, what they should report

description.en: Describe the situations worth raising with concrete examples from your own setting — a device left behind, a message that does not look right, information sent to the wrong person, an unexpected request for credentials, a door found open, a control that visibly is not working — and state plainly that a suspicion is enough and that being wrong carries no penalty. Attach the list.

evidenceHint.en: Reportable-situations list with worked examples in the language staff actually use

title.en: Decide the routes staff can report by and who receives each one

description.en: Settle the ways a person can raise something and, for each, name the role that receives it, the hours it is attended, and what happens outside those hours. Include at least one route that still works when the usual systems are unavailable. Record too the position taken on a report made without the reporter naming themselves — whether a route exists for that and which one, or that none does and why — so the choice is a visible decision rather than an assumption. Attach the route list with the receiving role and attended hours against each entry.

evidenceHint.en: Route list with the receiving role and attended hours per route, the alternative used when systems are unavailable, and the recorded position on unnamed reports

title.en: Write down what a reporter is told afterwards and what protection they have

description.en: Commit to what happens from the reporter's side: the acknowledgement they get and how quickly, what they are told about the outcome, and the organisation's stated position on a good-faith report that turns out to be nothing or that concerns a colleague or a manager. Attach the commitment together with the wording actually used when acknowledging a report.

evidenceHint.en: Written reporter commitment plus the acknowledgement wording used in practice

title.en: Publish the routes in the places people will be when they need them

description.en: Put the routes where the situation will find the person rather than where the security material lives — at the point of joining, where day-to-day work is discussed, and on or near the equipment and premises concerned. Attach the record of every place a route is published, with the date it went up and the person who maintains it, so a stale or removed notice is a visible row rather than a silent gap.

evidenceHint.en: Record of every place a reporting route is published, with the date it went up and who maintains it

title.en: Log every report received, including the ones that turn out to be nothing

description.en: Capture each report as it arrives: the route it came by, the time received, what was described, who took it, and where it went next. Keep the ones closed as no issue in the same log — they are the evidence that the route is trusted and used. Attach the report log for the period, or a nil return if nothing was raised.

evidenceHint.en: Report log for the period (or a nil return): route, time received, what was described, who took it, and where it went next

title.en: Raise a report down every published route and record how long it took to reach its receiver

description.en: Send an unannounced test report by each route on the list, including the one that works when the usual systems are unavailable and any route the list records as usable without the reporter naming themselves, and record when it was sent and when the named receiving role actually had it in hand. Attach the per-route test record together with the fix applied to any route that lost the report or took longer than the commitment made to reporters allows.

evidenceHint.en: Per-route test record with send and receipt times, and the fix applied to any route that failed or was slow

templates.title: Physical security perimeters
templates.description: Define and protect physical security perimeters

title.en: Record where each security perimeter runs and what it encloses

description.en: For every site the organisation occupies, set down the line of each security perimeter and name the areas, rooms and facilities that fall inside it, so that every protected area is enclosed by a stated boundary. The record may be a marked plan or a written description of the boundary — either is acceptable provided the line and the areas inside it can be identified from it. Attach the boundary record for each site.

evidenceHint.en: Boundary record per site — marked plan or written description — naming the areas each perimeter encloses

title.en: Record what forms each stretch of perimeter and every opening through it

description.en: Work along each boundary line in turn and set down, stretch by stretch, what physically separates inside from outside and its present condition, then list every opening through it — doorways, windows, hatches, loading points, ducts and service routes. Mark each stretch and each opening as adequate for what it encloses or as a shortfall. Attach the perimeter register.

evidenceHint.en: Perimeter register with one row per stretch and opening, its condition, and whether it is adequate

title.en: Close the perimeter shortfalls the register names

description.en: Take the stretches and openings the register marks as a shortfall and settle each one — by strengthening it, closing it, replacing it, or accepting it with a stated compensating arrangement and the reason. For each, record what was decided, what was done, who did it and when. Attach the remediation record, referencing the register rows it clears.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record naming each shortfall, the action taken, the person responsible and the date

title.en: Record each change to a perimeter and bring the register up to date

description.en: Whenever a boundary is altered — a new opening made, a stretch removed or breached for works, a partition moved, an area brought inside or taken outside a perimeter — record what changed, how the boundary was held while it was open, when it was reinstated, and amend the boundary record and perimeter register to match. Attach the change entries for the period with the amended register rows.

evidenceHint.en: Perimeter change entries for the period, each showing the interim arrangement and the register rows amended

title.en: Walk each perimeter and report where it differs from the register

description.en: Go round the boundary of each site and check, stretch by stretch, that what the register describes is what is actually there — present, intact, closing and fastening as recorded, with no undocumented opening. Record every difference found, what it exposes, and how it was resolved. Attach the inspection report per site.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection report per site listing each difference from the register and its resolution

templates.title: Physical entry
templates.description: Control physical access to secure areas

title.en: Record who is entitled to enter each controlled area and on what basis

description.en: For each area that is not open to everyone, set down which roles and which named individuals may enter, whether they may do so unaccompanied, and what gives them the entitlement — the job they hold, the contract they are under, the task they are engaged on. Attach the entitlement record covering every controlled area.

evidenceHint.en: Entry entitlement record per area, naming the role or individual, whether unaccompanied, and the basis

title.en: Record how entitlement is checked at each entry point before someone is admitted

description.en: For every point at which a person can enter a controlled area, set down who or what establishes that the person arriving is entitled to be admitted, what happens when they are not, and who may admit somebody outside the normal check. Describe the arrangement as it actually operates, whatever form it takes. Attach the record covering each entry point, including any point where no check is made.

evidenceHint.en: Per-entry-point record of who or what checks entitlement, the refusal handling and the override authority

title.en: Set out the terms on which people without their own entitlement are admitted

description.en: Write down the conditions under which visitors, contractors, delivery and collection staff and anyone else without an entitlement of their own is let into a controlled area: what identification is established, who authorises the admission, whether they are accompanied and by whom, and what is written down when they arrive and when they leave. Attach the admission terms together with the blank form the record will be kept on.

evidenceHint.en: Admission terms for non-entitled people, plus the blank record form they will be entered on

title.en: Record each admission of someone without their own entitlement

description.en: For every person admitted during the period on the terms above, capture the area entered, who authorised the admission, who accompanied them if anyone did, and the times of arrival and departure. Attach the completed admission records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Completed admission records for the period showing area, authoriser, accompaniment and times in and out

title.en: Withdraw entry entitlement when the need for it ends, and record the withdrawal

description.en: When somebody leaves, changes role, or finishes the work that gave them entitlement, remove their ability to enter the areas concerned — recovering whatever they hold that admits them and striking them from the entitlement record — and note the date and who did it. Attach the withdrawal records for the period beside the list of leavers, role changes and completed engagements they answer to.

evidenceHint.en: Withdrawal records for the period, matched to the leavers, role changes and ended engagements they correspond to

title.en: Compare who can actually get in against the entitlement record

description.en: Take each controlled area and establish who is in a position to enter it in practice, then set that against the entitlement record. List everyone who can enter without an entitlement and everyone entitled who no longer needs it, and record what was done about each. Attach the comparison and its outcomes.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison per area listing every discrepancy between actual and recorded entitlement, with its resolution

title.en: Record what each office, room and facility holds and the protection it therefore needs

description.en: Go through the rooms and facilities in use and set down, for each, the information, equipment and activities it contains and, from that, the protection the room itself must provide — how it is closed and fastened, what may be stored in it, whether it may be left unattended, and what separation it needs from neighbouring space. Attach the room record.

evidenceHint.en: Room record naming each room, what it holds and the protection the room is required to provide

title.en: Remove the public indications of where sensitive rooms are and what they hold

description.en: Find where the location or purpose of a sensitive room is announced to people with no need to know it — signage and wayfinding, internal and external directories, published plans, delivery addressing, listings in the organisation's own materials — and change or remove each one. Attach a record of what was found and what was done to it, showing the state before and after.

evidenceHint.en: Record of each public indication found and the change made to it, with before and after

title.en: Bring each room up to the protection its record requires

description.en: Take the rooms whose present state falls short of the room record and settle each shortfall — by providing the storage, fastening, separation or restriction the record calls for, by moving what is held into a room that already meets it, or by revising the requirement with a stated reason and who agreed it. Attach the remediation record per room.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record per room naming the shortfall, the action taken and the date

title.en: Record every room found left open or otherwise not secured as required

description.en: Whenever a room in the record is found unattended without the securing its record calls for — standing open, fastening not engaged, protective arrangement not in use — note the room, who found it, when, what was not secured, and how the room was made secure again. Attach the findings for the period, including the occasions on which nothing was found.

evidenceHint.en: Securing findings for the period naming the room, the state it was found in and how it was made secure

title.en: Check each room record against how the room is now used

description.en: Rooms change hands and change purpose. Go through the room record and confirm, room by room, that what it says the room holds is still true and that the protection stated is still the protection needed; where it is not, say what changed and raise an action. Attach the review listing the rooms whose holdings or required protection have moved, with the action raised for each.

evidenceHint.en: Review listing the rooms whose holdings or required protection changed, with the action raised for each

title.en: Record which areas are watched for unauthorised access and how each is watched

description.en: Set down the areas, entry points and approaches kept under observation for people being where they should not be, and for each one how that observation is achieved and when it applies — continuously, out of hours, on rounds. Name plainly any area in scope that is not watched at all. Attach the monitoring record.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring record naming each watched area, how it is observed, when, and the areas left unwatched

title.en: Record who is told when something is observed, and what they are to do

description.en: For each kind of observation the monitoring can produce — somebody in an area out of hours, an entry forced or held open, an unaccompanied stranger, an area that should be occupied standing empty — set down who is told, by what route, and what they are expected to do, including the point at which they pass it to somebody else. Attach the response record covering every kind of observation.

evidenceHint.en: Response record per kind of observation, naming the recipient, the route and the action expected

title.en: Record how what the monitoring captures is kept and who may see it

description.en: State where the material the monitoring produces is held, how long it is kept before disposal, who is permitted to view or release it and on what grounds, and how a request to view it is authorised and recorded. Attach the statement together with the current list of people permitted to view.

evidenceHint.en: Retention and access statement for monitoring material, with the list of people currently permitted to view it

title.en: Record every observation of possible unauthorised access and how it was dealt with

description.en: Capture each occasion during the period on which the monitoring produced something needing a response, including the ones that turned out to be innocent: what was observed, where, when, who responded, what they found, and how it ended. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring log for the period, each entry with the observation, the responder, the finding and the outcome

title.en: Confirm each area is still being watched the way its record says

description.en: Take the monitoring record area by area and establish that the observation it describes is actually happening now — that rounds are being made where rounds are the arrangement, that what should be in view is in view and not obstructed, that what should be captured is being captured, and that it reaches the person named in the response record. Note every arrangement found not working and the repair made. Attach the verification record.

evidenceHint.en: Verification record per monitored area, with how it was checked, the faults found and their repair

templates.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats

title.en: Record the physical and environmental threats each site is exposed to

description.en: For every site, set down the natural and man-made threats it could suffer — fire, water, storm, ground movement, extremes of temperature, explosion or damage arising from activity nearby, disruption of the surrounding area — reasoning from the site's location, construction, neighbours and history. For each threat, record what would be affected and how badly. Attach the exposure record per site.

evidenceHint.en: Exposure record per site naming each threat, the areas and assets exposed and the effect expected

title.en: Map each recorded threat to the protection that answers it

description.en: Take the exposure record and set against each threat whatever already stands between it and what it would affect — construction, separation, distance, detection, suppression, drainage, containment, or an arrangement with somebody else to act — and name who is responsible for keeping that protection working. Name plainly every threat with nothing against it. Attach the protection register.

evidenceHint.en: Protection register linking each threat to the protection in place and its owner, with unprotected threats named

title.en: Settle each threat the protection register leaves uncovered

description.en: For every threat the register names as having nothing against it, record the outcome reached: the protection introduced, the reduction of what is exposed at that site, or a stated decision to accept the exposure with the reason and the name of whoever accepted it. Attach the record covering every uncovered threat, referencing the register rows it clears.

evidenceHint.en: Record per uncovered threat of the protection introduced or the exposure accepted, with who decided and when

title.en: Show that each protection against the site's threats still stands

description.en: Work down the protection register and record, for every entry, what was done or observed during the period to establish that the protection is still doing its job. Where the protection is something that operates — a detector, a suppression system, a pump, a barrier that has to be worked — that is the inspection, test, service, replenishment or replacement, with the date, who did it, the result, and any fault raised and its repair. Where the protection is inherent in the site — its construction, the level it sits at, the distance or open ground between it and the hazard — that is a confirmation that the condition is unchanged, with the date and who checked. Where somebody else provides it, attach what they supplied. Attach the record for the period with every register row accounted for.

evidenceHint.en: Record for the period accounting for every protection register row: the service or test result, the confirmation the inherent condition is unchanged, or what the provider supplied

title.en: Reassess site exposure against the changes made at and around each site

description.en: List what changed at or around each site during the period — building work, a change of use, new neighbouring activity, an event that actually occurred and what it did — and say for each whether it alters the exposure record or the protection register. Update both where it does, and raise an action wherever the protection no longer matches the exposure. Attach the reassessment.

evidenceHint.en: Reassessment naming each change, its effect on exposure, and the register updates or actions raised

templates.title: Working in secure areas
templates.description: Define procedures for working in secure areas

title.en: Record the work carried out inside each secure area and who performs it

description.en: For every area the organisation treats as secure, write down what work actually happens inside it, which roles perform that work, what equipment or materials are taken in to do it, and whether any of it is done by people from outside the organisation or by someone working alone. Build this from asking the people who use the area rather than from an assumption about its purpose. Attach the activity record, one section per secure area.

evidenceHint.en: Activity record per secure area naming the work, the roles performing it and the equipment taken in

title.en: State the rules of conduct that apply inside each secure area

description.en: Turn the activity record into written rules for behaviour inside the area: what may be brought in and what may be taken out, the position on recording and capture of what is visible there, when work may proceed without a second person present, what applies to people from outside the organisation, and what must be done when the area is left with nobody in it. Write a rule only where the activity record shows the situation arises. Attach the rules with the areas each one covers.

evidenceHint.en: The secure-area conduct rules, showing which areas each rule covers

title.en: Record how each person working in a secure area is made aware of its rules

description.en: For every person who works in a secure area — employed or not — record that the rules for that area were put in front of them before they first worked there, by whatever means the organisation uses, and hold their confirmation that they received them. Attach the awareness record naming the person, the area, the date and the means used, covering everyone the activity record says works there.

evidenceHint.en: Awareness record naming person, area, date and the means by which the rules were given

title.en: Log the work done in secure areas by people from outside the organisation and by people working alone

description.en: Keep a running record of each occasion someone from outside the organisation, or someone working without a second person present, carries out work inside a secure area. Capture the area, the work done, the person, who was accountable for them while they were inside, and the period they were there. Attach the log covering the reporting period.

evidenceHint.en: Secure-area work log for the period, with area, worker, activity and the person accountable

title.en: Check observed conduct in secure areas against the stated rules

description.en: Attend secure areas while work is under way, without giving notice, and compare what is actually being done against the rules written for that area — what has been brought in, whether work that needs a second person has one, whether the area is left as the rules require. Record each departure from the rules, who it was raised with and what changed. Attach the check report.

evidenceHint.en: Check report listing each departure from the rules observed and the action taken

templates.title: Clear desk and clear screen
templates.description: Implement clear desk and screen policy

title.en: List the desks, shared points and screens the clear desk rules must cover

description.en: Walk the places where people work and where information ends up waiting: fixed and shared desks, meeting and interview rooms, print and collection points, post trays, whiteboards, and any screen that faces a space the organisation does not control. For each, note what kind of information is handled there and what is available today for putting it away. Attach the resulting scope list.

evidenceHint.en: Scope list of workspaces, shared points and screens, with what is handled at each and the storage available

title.en: State what must be put away and what a screen must show when a workspace is left unattended

description.en: Write the rules against the situations in the scope list rather than as a general principle: a desk left at the end of the day, a desk left for a short period, a meeting room vacated, output waiting at a collection point, a whiteboard after a discussion, a screen left with nobody in front of it. Say for each what must not remain visible or reachable. Attach the published rules with the situation each covers.

evidenceHint.en: Published clear desk and clear screen rules, written per situation

title.en: Record where the material held at each workspace is put when it is left unattended

description.en: Go through the scope list and, for every area, record the destination its papers and portable items go to when the workspace is left — a container at the desk, a room used for the purpose, a return to a central holding point, or a rule that such material is not handled there at all.
