Where the recorded destination did not exist, record what was provided or what handling changed instead. Attach the per-area record with any area still unresolved.

evidenceHint.en: Per-area record naming where unattended material is secured, and the areas still unresolved

title.en: Record how each class of screen is made unreadable when left unattended

description.en: For every class of workstation, shared terminal and fixed display in scope, record what makes the screen unreadable once nobody is in front of it — an unattended period after which it locks itself, an action the user is required to take, sign-out at a shared machine, or how the display is positioned — and the setting or instruction that delivers it. Attach the record covering every class in the scope list, including any class nothing currently reaches.

evidenceHint.en: Record per screen class of what makes it unreadable when unattended and the setting or instruction behind it

title.en: Record what is found left exposed when workspaces are checked

description.en: Walk the areas in scope while they are unoccupied and note what has been left in view or within reach against the rules for that situation: documents, portable items, keys, whiteboard content and unattended screens. Record the area, what was found, what was done with it and the follow-up with whoever left it. Attach the record of each check made in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Check record per walk, naming the area, what was found exposed and the follow-up

title.en: Check that screens are in fact unreadable by the means recorded for their class

description.en: Take a sample of screens across every class in the screen record and establish, for each, whether it is genuinely unreadable when nobody is in front of it — testing it the way its own record says it works. Where the record relies on an unattended period, leave the screen and wait it out. Where it relies on an action the user takes, take screens their users have left and see whether the recorded instruction produced an unreadable screen. Where it relies on signing out at a shared machine, look at what that machine shows between users. Where it relies on how the display faces, read it from the space it can be seen from. Include screens that sit outside whatever normally applies the class, since those are the ones most likely to differ. Attach the sample check listing each screen, how it was tested, what was found and whether it matched its class record.

evidenceHint.en: Sample check listing each screen, how it was tested against its class record, the result observed and whether it matched

title.en: Map the physical location of every item of information-processing equipment

description.en: Walk each site and record, for every server, network device, workstation, printer and screen, the building, room and rack or desk it occupies. Note alongside each entry the hazards present at that spot: overlooking from public areas, water pipes overhead, external windows, proximity to loading or delivery routes, heat sources. Attach the completed siting register as evidence.

evidenceHint.en: Siting register listing each equipment item, its room/rack location, and the hazards observed at that location

title.en: Record the siting rules that apply to each class of equipment

description.en: Write down, per equipment class and location type, what siting is acceptable: screen orientation away from windows and public sightlines, minimum clearance from water and drainage runs, restriction of rack rooms to authorised entry, separation from delivery and loading areas. Ground each rule in a hazard actually observed in the siting register rather than a generic list. Attach the siting standard.

evidenceHint.en: Siting standard giving the acceptable placement conditions per equipment class

title.en: Reposition or shield the equipment whose placement breaches the siting rules

description.en: Take the register entries that fail the siting standard and fix each one: move the unit, rotate or fit a privacy filter to the screen, install a drip tray or deflector, or relocate the rack. Where a move is not possible, record the compensating measure fitted. Evidence is a remediation record per non-conforming item showing the before state, the action taken and who signed it off.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record per non-conforming item with the action taken and sign-off

title.en: Check the siting rules on every equipment installation or move

description.en: Make the siting check a recorded step in the equipment move and install process: before the unit is powered on at its new spot, the engineer records the location, confirms it against the siting standard and updates the siting register. Run this for every move in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Equipment move and install log for the period, each entry carrying the siting check outcome and the register update

title.en: Inspect each equipment location against the siting register

description.en: Walk the sites again and compare what is physically present against the register: equipment that has moved without a record, new units not registered, screens that have been turned, shielding that has been removed. Record each deviation and how it was resolved. Attach the inspection sheet with the deviation list.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection sheet listing deviations found between the floor and the register, with resolution per deviation

title.en: List every asset authorised to be taken off the premises and who holds it

description.en: Enumerate the laptops, mobile devices, portable media, and any equipment issued for home working, travel or client sites. For each, record the holder, the type of destination it is authorised for, and the classification of information it carries or can reach. Attach the off-premises asset register.

evidenceHint.en: Off-premises asset register: asset id, holder, authorised destination type, information classification

title.en: Record the protection required for each class of off-premises asset

description.en: State per asset class what must be in place before it leaves: full-disk encryption, screen lock timeout, privacy filter, physical lock, the rule on leaving equipment unattended in vehicles or hotel rooms, and what the holder does if it is lost. Derive the classes from the register rather than writing a generic mobile-working policy. Attach the handling standard.

evidenceHint.en: Off-premises handling standard mapping each required protective measure to an asset class

title.en: Set up the check-out approval step for removing an asset from the premises

description.en: Put in place the form or workflow that captures, before an asset leaves, who is taking it, where, for how long, and the approval. Include the confirmation that the protections required for that asset class are in place. Attach the form or workflow configuration together with one completed example.

evidenceHint.en: The check-out form or workflow definition plus one completed check-out record

title.en: Record each asset removal and return in the check-out log

description.en: For every asset that leaves and comes back during the period, log the removal date, holder, destination, approver and the return date. Keep items still signed out visible as open entries so custody is known at any moment. Attach the log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Check-out log for the period showing removal, holder, approval and return date per asset

title.en: Reconcile the off-premises register against assets actually returned or still signed out

description.en: Compare the check-out log with the register and with physical or remote confirmation of each asset: items shown as returned that cannot be located, items long overdue, holders who have changed role. Record each discrepancy and what was done about it. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of the register against the check-out log, listing overdue and unaccounted assets and their resolution

title.en: Record every storage medium held, where it is and what information is on it

description.en: Enumerate the media the organisation holds as items in their own right — backup and archive media, portable drives, memory devices, cards, and disks that have been taken out of the equipment they served. Include media held away from the organisation's own sites and media carried in field or engineering kit. For each, record its identifier, its type, who holds it or where it sits, and the classification of the information written to it. Attach the media register.

evidenceHint.en: Media register: identifier, type, holder or location, and the classification of the information held

title.en: State the handling each media type and classification requires

description.en: For each combination of media type and information classification appearing in the register, write down what is required: how the information on it is protected against being read by someone who obtains the item, where it is kept when not in use, how it is identified so a holder knows what they have, how it is accompanied and tracked when it moves between holders or locations, and the point at which it must be taken out of use. Attach the handling rules.

evidenceHint.en: Media handling rules giving the protection, storage, identification, transfer and withdrawal requirement per type and classification

title.en: Bring the media already held into line with the handling rules

description.en: Work down the register item by item and record what was done to bring each one to the handling its type and classification calls for — how its information was protected, how it was identified, and where it was moved to. Where an item cannot meet the rule, record it as an exception with the handling put in its place and who accepted that. Attach the per-item record showing the state of every entry in the register.

evidenceHint.en: Per-item record showing what was applied to each registered medium, and each exception with its accepted alternative handling

title.en: Record each transfer of media so custody is unbroken

description.en: Log every movement in the period against the register entry it affects: a medium given to a person, moved between locations, sent to or recalled from a holding site, or handed to whoever carries it. Each entry names who released it, who received it and when, so the register can answer who holds any item at any moment. Attach the movement entries for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Media register movement entries for the period, naming releasing and receiving holder at each step

title.en: Close the register entry for each medium withdrawn from use

description.en: When a medium reaches the point of withdrawal the handling rules set, or fails before it, record why it was withdrawn, what became of the item, and what is held to show the information it carried can no longer be recovered from it, then mark the register entry closed. Run this so no withdrawn medium is left as an open entry. Attach the withdrawal entries for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Withdrawal entries for the period, each naming the reason, what became of the item and what shows its information is unrecoverable

title.en: Account for every medium the register lists

description.en: Confirm the presence of each open register entry at the location or with the holder it names, and identify media found that the register does not list. Record every difference — present but unregistered, registered but not found, held by someone other than the recorded holder — and how each was resolved. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of registered against present media, listing each discrepancy and its resolution

title.en: List the supporting utilities each information-processing facility depends on

description.en: For every site and equipment room, record the utilities it needs to keep running: mains feeds and their supply routes, HVAC and ventilation units, water and drainage, telecommunications circuits and their carriers. Note the rated capacity or supply limit of each. Attach the utility dependency list per facility.

evidenceHint.en: Utility dependency list per facility naming each supply, its provider or route, and its rated capacity

title.en: Record the protective equipment fitted against each utility dependency

description.en: Map each dependency in the list to what protects it: UPS units and their rated runtime, generators and fuel held, redundant power feeds, standby cooling, diverse telecoms routes. Where a dependency has no protection, record it as such rather than leaving it blank. Attach the mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Mapping of each utility dependency to its protective equipment, with rated runtime or capacity, and the unprotected dependencies named

title.en: Route utility failure alarms to a monitored destination

description.en: Configure the alarms on power, cooling and environmental sensors so a failure or threshold breach reaches somebody who is on duty — building management system, monitoring platform or paging rota. Trigger a test condition and confirm the alert was received. Attach the alarm configuration and the received test alert.

evidenceHint.en: Alarm configuration export plus evidence of a test alert being received by the on-duty destination

title.en: Record each utility inspection and protective-equipment test result

description.en: Run the inspections and load tests due in the period — UPS discharge, generator run, cooling service, sensor check — and record the date, the result including measured runtime or capacity, and any fault raised. Attach the test and inspection records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: UPS, generator, cooling and sensor test records for the period with dates, measured results and faults raised

title.en: Assess whether utility protection still covers each facility's current load

description.en: Compare the present electrical and cooling load of each equipment room against the rated capacity and the runtime measured in testing. Where load has grown past what the protection covers, record the shortfall and the action agreed. Attach the assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Capacity assessment comparing measured load against rated protection per facility, with shortfalls and agreed actions

title.en: Map the power and network cable routes serving each facility

description.en: Record where cabling runs: building entry points, risers, floor voids and ceiling runs, patch rooms and cabinets, and the circuits each route carries. Note where power and data share a route and where cable passes through areas outside the organisation's control. Attach the cable route plan or schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Cable route plan or schedule showing entry points, routes, patch rooms and the circuits carried

title.en: Label the cables and patch panel ports to match the cable schedule

description.en: Apply labels at both ends of each run and on every patch panel port so a cable can be identified without tracing it. The labels must use the same identifiers as the schedule. Attach photographs or a labelling record per patch panel and cabinet.

evidenceHint.en: Labelling record or photographs per patch panel showing labels matching the cable schedule identifiers

title.en: Protect the cable routes and patch rooms identified as exposed

description.en: Address the routes flagged in the mapping: fit conduit or trunking to accessible runs, lock patch cabinets and comms rooms, separate power from data cabling where induction or damage is a risk, and secure building entry points. Record what was fitted for each exposed segment. Attach the remediation record.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record naming each exposed cable segment or patch room and the protection fitted

title.en: Record each patching change against the cable schedule

description.en: Every time a port is patched, repatched or a run is added or removed, log the port, the circuit, the reason and the date, and update the cable schedule in the same step so the schedule stays true. Attach the patching log for the period alongside the updated schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Patching change log for the period with the corresponding cable schedule updates

title.en: Inspect patch rooms and accessible cable runs for undocumented connections

description.en: Physically inspect cabinets, risers and accessible runs looking for cables not on the schedule, unlabelled patches, taps or splitters, and unsecured cabinet doors. Record each unidentified cable and whether it was traced, removed or added to the schedule. Attach the inspection record.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection record listing every undocumented or unlabelled cable found and its disposition

title.en: Record which equipment must be serviced to stay available and when each service falls due

description.en: Identify the items the organisation depends on for its information processing that will degrade or fail without servicing, and for each record who is responsible for that servicing — an internal team or a named supplier and the agreement covering it — the interval at which it is to be serviced, what that interval was set from, and the date the next service falls due. Attach the maintenance schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance schedule: item, responsible party or agreement, service interval and its basis, next due date

title.en: State the conditions that apply to anyone servicing equipment and to the information it holds

description.en: Write down what governs work on the equipment in the schedule, whether it is done on site, remotely or after the item is taken away: how the person doing the work is confirmed to be who they claim, what access to the information held on the item the work requires and what they may do with it, whether the item or the storage inside it may leave the organisation's control, and what must be recorded when the work finishes. Where a supplier does the work, record where these conditions are written into the agreement with them. Attach the conditions with those references.

evidenceHint.en: The maintenance conditions document, with the clause references binding each supplier that services listed equipment

title.en: Record each maintenance job against the equipment it was carried out on

description.en: For every service carried out in the period, capture the date, who performed it, what was done, what was replaced, and anything the work revealed about the item's condition. File each record against the item in the schedule, so one item's history can be read in one place rather than assembled from separate reports. Attach the maintenance records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance records for the period filed against each item, with date, performer, work done and condition raised

title.en: Record the release and return of each item sent away for repair

description.en: For every item that leaves the organisation's control to be repaired, record what was done about the information held on it before it went — taken out, put beyond recovery, or left in place under the conditions that bind whoever receives it — together with who took it, when, and the date it came back or was written off instead. Keep items not yet returned visible as open entries. Attach the release and return records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Release and return records for items repaired away from the organisation, showing the information decision and the return date or open status

title.en: Report the services that fell due and were not carried out

description.en: Compare the due dates in the schedule against the maintenance records for the period and list every service that did not happen when it should have. For each, record why it slipped, what running that item unserviced means for the availability it supports, and the date agreed to bring it back into schedule. Attach the report with those agreed dates.

evidenceHint.en: Overdue-service report naming each missed service, the reason, the availability consequence and the agreed recovery date

templates.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment

title.en: List the equipment awaiting disposal or re-use and the storage it contains

description.en: Identify every retired or pending-reissue item currently held — laptops, servers, disks pulled from arrays, network devices with configuration in flash, printers and multifunction devices with internal drives. Record the asset id, the storage components inside it, and the classification of data that reached the device. Attach the disposal queue.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal queue listing asset id, the storage components held inside each item, and the data classification

title.en: Record the sanitisation method required for each storage type and classification

description.en: State which method applies to which media and classification: multi-pass overwrite, cryptographic erase where the device was encrypted from first use, degaussing, or physical destruction. Include embedded storage such as printer drives and device flash, and say what verification counts as proof for each method. Attach the sanitisation standard.

evidenceHint.en: Sanitisation standard mapping storage type and data classification to the required method and its verification

title.en: Verify and record the sanitisation of each device before it leaves the organisation

description.en: Apply the method the standard requires, then capture the proof: the wipe tool's completion report, the crypto-erase confirmation, or the destruction certificate with serial numbers. Hold the item until that record exists, so nothing leaves on trust. Attach the verification records referencing asset ids.

evidenceHint.en: Per-device sanitisation verification record — tool output, erase confirmation or destruction certificate — referencing the asset id

title.en: Record the destination of every item disposed of or returned to use

description.en: Log where each item went: the recycler or disposal contractor and their receipt, the leased-equipment return, or the internal reissue and its new holder. Keep the receipt or transfer note against the asset id so the chain does not end at the loading bay. Attach the disposal register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal register for the period with recipient, date and the contractor receipt or reissue record per asset

title.en: Reconcile the disposal register against the assets retired from the inventory

description.en: Take every asset marked retired, reissued or written off in the period and confirm each has a matching sanitisation verification and a recorded destination. Record assets retired with neither, and how each gap was closed. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of retired assets against sanitisation and disposal records, listing gaps and their resolution

title.en: Inventory the endpoint devices that hold or reach organisational information

description.en: Enumerate every laptop, desktop, tablet and phone used for work, recording holder, operating system version, and whether it is corporate-owned or personal. Pull the list from the device-management console and reconcile it with HR's headcount so unenrolled devices surface. Attach the inventory itself.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint device inventory listing holder, OS version, ownership and management state per device

title.en: Record the required security configuration for each class of endpoint device

description.en: Write down, per device class in the inventory (corporate laptop, mobile, personal device), what must be true: disk encryption, screen-lock timeout, patch level, malware protection, and whether local administrator rights are permitted. State the reasoning where a class is treated differently. Attach the configuration standard.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint configuration standard, one settings block per device class

title.en: Enforce disk encryption and screen lock on every enrolled endpoint

description.en: Apply the standard's encryption and lock settings as policy in the device-management platform rather than device by device, then export the per-device compliance state and drive the non-compliant devices to compliance. Attach the export plus a note on any device that could not be brought into line and why.

evidenceHint.en: Device-management console export showing encryption and lock state per device, with exceptions annotated

title.en: Record enrolment and de-enrolment of endpoints as users join and leave

description.en: For each period, capture which devices were enrolled and which were wiped or de-enrolled, tied to the joiner or leaver that triggered it. This is what shows a departed user's device stopped reaching organisational information. Attach the log.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint enrolment and de-enrolment log for the period, each entry linked to its joiner or leaver event

title.en: Reconcile the endpoint inventory against the device-management console

description.en: Compare the inventory to the devices actually reporting in, and list devices present in one and not the other. For each discrepancy record the disposition — enrolled, retired, or accepted with a reason. Attach the reconciliation, not just a statement that it was done.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation showing unmanaged and orphaned devices with a disposition against each

title.en: Inventory the privileged accounts and administrative roles in every in-scope system

description.en: For each system, list the accounts and roles that can change configuration, grant access, or read data across users — including cloud console roles, database superusers, domain administrators, and shared or break-glass accounts. Record the holder for each. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Privileged access register: system, account or role, privilege granted, named holder

title.en: Record who authorises each privileged role and for how long it is held

description.en: Against each role in the register, state who may approve a grant, whether the grant is standing or time-bound, and the conditions for use of break-glass accounts. Where a role is standing, record why time-bounding is not workable. Attach the resulting privileged-access rules.

evidenceHint.en: Privileged access rules document mapping each role to its approver and grant duration

title.en: Separate privileged accounts from their holders' everyday user accounts

description.en: Give each administrator a distinct identity for privileged work so routine email and browsing never run with elevated rights, and remove privilege from the day-to-day account. Attach a directory export showing the pairing, and note any system that cannot support separation together with the compensating measure.

evidenceHint.en: Directory export pairing each administrator's standard account with a separate privileged identity

title.en: Record each grant and revocation of privileged access with its authorisation

description.en: Log every elevation and removal as it happens, capturing who requested it, who approved it, the system, and the date it was withdrawn. Break-glass use is logged the same way with the reason for invoking it. Attach the log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Privileged access grant and revocation log for the period, including break-glass invocations

title.en: Recertify every privileged account against the register and withdraw those no longer justified

description.en: Put the current holder list for each privileged role in front of the system owner, have them confirm or reject each holder, and remove the rejected ones. Record what was removed and when, so the recertification shows an outcome rather than a signature. Attach the recertification with removals evidenced.

evidenceHint.en: Recertification record showing confirm or remove per privileged account and the completed removals

templates.title: Information access restriction
templates.description: Restrict access to information per policy

title.en: Map each class of information to the roles permitted to read and to change it

description.en: Build a matrix whose rows are information classes or repositories and whose columns are business roles, marking read, write and no-access in each cell. Agree it with the owner of each information class rather than deriving it from what access currently exists. Attach the matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Access matrix of information classes against roles, showing read, write or no access per cell

title.en: Configure system permissions so each role sees only what its matrix row allows

description.en: Translate the matrix into the actual permission model of each system holding the information — groups, roles, sharing settings — and remove access that exceeds the row. Attach a permission export per system alongside the matrix row it implements, so a reviewer can compare them.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system permission export placed beside the matrix row it implements

title.en: Restrict bulk export and reporting of restricted information to named roles

description.en: Identify the routes that yield information in bulk — report builders, database query tools, data exports, integration credentials — and limit them to the roles the matrix permits, so read access to a record does not become read access to the population. Attach the configuration showing who retains bulk export.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration record of bulk export and reporting rights, listing the roles that retain them

title.en: Record every access-rule change against the request that authorised it

description.en: As permissions are granted, altered or withdrawn, log the system, the principal, what changed, who asked and who approved. This is what makes an unexpected permission traceable later. Attach the change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Access-rule change log for the period, each entry carrying its requester and approver

title.en: Test a sample of accounts against the access matrix and report the deviations

description.en: Pick accounts across several roles, enumerate what each can actually reach in the live systems, and compare it to the matrix row for that role. Record every deviation with its cause — stale grant, over-broad group, matrix wrong — and the correction made. Attach the test results.

evidenceHint.en: Access test results per sampled account: expected access, actual access, deviation and correction

title.en: Register the source code holdings and every copy kept outside them

description.en: Work outward from the code the organisation builds and runs: name each store that holds it and the owner of that store. Then record the copies living outside those stores — working copies on developer machines, archived or escrowed snapshots, and code handed to a third party — because a copy carries none of the store's restrictions with it. Attach the register with one row per holding and per copy.

evidenceHint.en: Source code register: each holding and each copy, with its owner and location

title.en: Record who may read, change and administer each source code holding

description.en: For every row of the register decide three separate things: who may read the code, who may change it, and who may alter the holding's own permissions and settings. Cover non-human identities explicitly — build, deployment and integration accounts hold change rights and are the ones usually left off the model. Attach the permission model.

evidenceHint.en: Permission model naming read, change and administer holders per holding, including non-human identities

title.en: Apply the recorded permissions at each holding and withdraw the access beyond them

description.en: Set each holding's permissions to match the model by whatever means that holding provides, and remove access exceeding the model rather than leaving it noted as an exception. Where a holding cannot express the model, record the restriction relied on instead and who owns it. Attach the resulting permission listing per holding together with the record of what was withdrawn.

evidenceHint.en: Per-holding permission listing after alignment, with the list of access withdrawn

title.en: Record each grant and withdrawal of source code access in the period

description.en: Log every addition and removal of access as people and services arrive, change role or leave, naming the holding, the identity, the level granted or removed, and what prompted it. Include credentials issued to or retired from automated identities, which change hands without anyone joining or leaving. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Source code access change log for the period, including non-human identities

title.en: Reconcile the accounts and copies holding source code against who needs them now

description.en: Put the register and the current permission listings beside the people and services actually doing the work. Name every account that is no longer needed, every copy nobody will claim, and every third party still holding code beyond its purpose, and record the withdrawal or destruction of each. Attach the reconciliation with an outcome against every line.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of source code access holders and copies against current need, with outcome per line

title.en: Record how each system establishes that a user or service is who they claim to be

description.en: For every in-scope system record where the identity is verified — centrally or by the system itself — what proof it demands before a session begins, and how non-human identities authenticate to it. Attach the register; its value is that it makes visible the systems that accept a single shared secret and nothing more.

evidenceHint.en: Authentication register: system, where identity is verified, proof demanded, and method used by non-human identities

title.en: Set how many independent proofs a sign-in must present for each class of system

description.en: State per class how many independent proofs a sign-in must present and of what kinds, how long a session may run before identity is established again, and what must happen after repeated failed attempts. Where the organisation has separately recorded what makes a secret or credential strong enough, reference that record rather than restating the requirement here. Record a justification for every class held below the general requirement. Attach the requirement statement.

evidenceHint.en: Authentication requirement statement per system class, with a justification for each class held below it

title.en: Bring each registered system up to the proof its class requires

description.en: Work through the register row by row, changing what each system demands at sign-in until it matches its class, and record every row still short of the requirement with an owner and a date. Attach, per system, evidence of what is now demanded, alongside the outstanding list — the list is as much the deliverable as the settings are.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system evidence of the proof now demanded at sign-in, plus the list of systems still short with owner and date

title.en: Record every change made this period to what a system demands at sign-in

description.en: Whenever a system enters the authentication register, changes the proof it demands, or is granted or released from a justification for sitting below its class requirement, record the system, its class, what was demanded before and what is demanded now, who decided and why. Where a class saw no change in the period, record that rather than leaving it out. Attach the change record for the period together with the register rows it updates.

evidenceHint.en: Change record for the period: system, class, the proof demanded before and after, the decider and the reason, with the classes that saw no change stated as such

title.en: Attempt sign-in against a sample of systems and record what was actually demanded

description.en: Pick systems across the classes and try to sign in: confirm the proofs the requirement names are genuinely demanded, that repeated failure is answered as stated, and that a session does not outlive the period allowed. Record observed against expected behaviour for each system, and the fix for every deviation. Attach the test record.

evidenceHint.en: Sign-in test record per sampled system: expected proof, observed behaviour, deviation and fix

title.en: List the finite resources whose exhaustion would degrade a service

description.en: Work back from each service in scope to the things it can run out of: processing, memory and storage, connection or record limits, network throughput, licence seats, and the people who are the constraint where no substitute exists. Give each a measure, its present level and its ceiling. Attach the capacity register.

evidenceHint.en: Capacity register: resource, service it constrains, measure, present level and ceiling

title.en: Set the level at which each resource must be acted on, and the action it triggers

description.en: For every register row decide the level that obliges somebody to act and the level at which the service is at risk, and name the action each triggers — add capacity, move or shed load, remove data, obtain more seats. Size the acting level to how long that resource genuinely takes to add, not to a round number. Attach the threshold list.

evidenceHint.en: Threshold list per resource: acting level, at-risk level, and the action each triggers

title.en: Record how each capacity threshold is observed and who is told when it is crossed

description.en: For every register row state how the level is established — a continuously collected figure, a periodic report, a supplier's statement, a reading somebody takes — at what interval it is established, and the named recipient who is told when a threshold is crossed. Attach the table; a row with no observer against it is the finding it exists to produce.

evidenceHint.en: Observation table mapping every register row to its observation method, interval and named recipient

title.en: Report the level each resource reached this period and what was done at every crossing

description.en: Bring together the period's figures for the register's resources, list every threshold crossing, and record against each what was done: capacity added, load moved, or the crossing accepted with a stated reason and a named person accepting it. Attach the report so an unactioned crossing is visible rather than absent.

evidenceHint.en: Capacity report for the period: level reached per resource, every crossing, and the action closing each

title.en: Project known demand against present capacity and record the provisioning decisions

description.en: Take the growth already committed — customer or headcount commitments, planned launches, data accumulating under retention rules — and work out the date each resource reaches its ceiling at that rate. Record the decision for each and when it has to start, given the lead time behind its acting level. Attach the forecast with its decisions.

evidenceHint.en: Capacity forecast: projected demand, expected exhaustion date, and the decision and start date per resource

title.en: List the routes by which code and files reach the organisation's systems

description.en: Name every way something executable or file-borne arrives: messages and attachments, downloads and browsing, removable media and physical transfer, shared and collaboration spaces, software and components drawn from outside, and connections opened by suppliers. Record which systems each route reaches. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of arrival routes with the systems each route reaches

title.en: Record the malware defence in place for each system and route in the register

description.en: Against each register row record what stands between an arriving item and its execution — detection on the system or at the route, restriction of what is permitted to run, inspection before the item is opened, or isolation of the receiving system — with who maintains that defence and how it is kept current. Rows with nothing against them are the output that matters. Attach the defence register.

evidenceHint.en: Defence register: the defence recorded against each system and route, or that row named as undefended

title.en: Record what happens when malicious code is found and who decides each step

description.en: Write the handling path: who is told, on what basis a system is taken out of use, who establishes that it is fit to return, what is done about anything the item may have reached, and the point at which the case is treated as an incident. Name roles rather than individuals so the path survives staff changes. Attach the procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Handling procedure naming the deciding roles and the removal-from-use and return-to-use criteria

title.en: Record every suspected and confirmed malicious code event this period

description.en: Log each event whatever raised it — a defence that stopped or quarantined something, a person reporting a suspicious item, a supplier notification — with the system affected, what was found, what was done, and how the case closed. Items stopped before reaching a system count, and are the evidence the defence works. Attach the log.

evidenceHint.en: Malicious code event log for the period: system, what was found, action taken and closure

title.en: Check each recorded defence is in the state the register claims, and list those that are not

description.en: Go back over the defence register and establish for every row that what it records is genuinely present, still covering the systems named, and still being kept current by the person named. Record every row that fails that check together with the remediation against it and its date. Attach the verification.

evidenceHint.en: Verification of the defence register listing failing rows with remediation and date against each

title.en: Name the source that announces vulnerabilities for each technology in use

description.en: Take the technologies the organisation runs — operating systems, infrastructure and network products, databases, application platforms, and the components applications depend on — and record for each the source that would announce a weakness in it and the named person who receives that source. Attach the table; technologies with no source against them are the gap this task exists to expose.

evidenceHint.en: Technology-to-source table with the named recipient against each source, unwatched technologies visible

title.en: Record how a vulnerability is rated and what response each band requires

description.en: Write down what the rating takes into account — the severity as published, how exposed the affected system is, whether the weakness is known to be in use, and what the system holds — and the bands it produces. Against each band record the response required, whether to correct, to reduce by other means, or to accept, the elapsed time allowed, and who may accept. Attach the scheme.

evidenceHint.en: Rating scheme giving the bands, the response and elapsed time allowed for each, and the accepting role

title.en: Assess the estate against the vulnerabilities made known this period

description.en: Match what the sources announced during the period against the products and versions actually running, and produce the list of systems affected. Record the parts of the estate that could not be assessed and why, so that absence from the result is never read as cleanliness. Attach the assessment together with that exclusion list.

evidenceHint.en: Assessment result for the period: affected systems, plus what could not be assessed and the reason

title.en: Record the disposition of every vulnerability identified this period

description.en: Give each identified vulnerability exactly one outcome: corrected, reduced by another named measure, or accepted with a stated justification and the person who accepted it. Record the date it reached that outcome, since an open item with no date is indistinguishable from a forgotten one. Attach the tracker with one line per vulnerability and affected system.

evidenceHint.en: Tracker export: one line per vulnerability with affected system, disposition, date reached and acceptor

title.en: Account for every asset that did not appear in this period's assessment

description.en: Put the assets that appeared in the assessment beside the organisation's asset inventory and name each one missing from it, with the reason — retired, out of scope, unreachable, or simply never covered — and the action taken. Attach the reconciliation; the difference between the two lists is the part of the estate this control did not reach.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of assessed assets against the asset inventory with a reason and action per missing asset

title.en: Measure the time taken from a vulnerability becoming known to its response completing

description.en: For the vulnerabilities closed during the period, measure the elapsed time between the source announcing it and the recorded response completing, and set that against the time its band allows. List every one that exceeded its allowance with the reason and what is being changed. Attach the measurement.

evidenceHint.en: Elapsed-time measurement per closed vulnerability against its band's allowance, with each overrun explained

title.en: List the platform types whose configuration is managed and the baseline governing each

description.en: Enumerate the platform and service types in use — operating systems, infrastructure and network devices, cloud services, databases, application platforms — with how many instances of each are running and which baseline of required settings governs it. Attach the list; a platform type with no baseline against it is the finding the list produces.

evidenceHint.en: Platform-type list with instance count and governing baseline, types with no baseline visible

title.en: Record the required value of each security-relevant setting per platform type

description.en: For each platform type on the list, write down the settings that bear on security and the value each must hold, and name the guidance or internal decision the value was taken from. Where the chosen value departs from its source, record why. Attach the baseline for each platform type.

evidenceHint.en: Baseline per platform type: setting, required value, and the source the value came from

title.en: Record how a new instance receives its baseline before it holds live information

description.en: State, per platform type, how a newly built instance comes to hold the required values and who confirms that it does before it carries live information or serves users. Attach the statement together with a worked example from the most recent instance built, whatever its date, showing that the confirmation actually happened; where no instance has been built since the process was written down, record that instead.

evidenceHint.en: Per-platform statement of how a new instance is brought to baseline, with the confirmation from the most recent build or a record that none has been built since

title.en: Record every change made to a baseline definition, with its author and reason

description.en: Whenever a required value is added to, altered in, or dropped from a baseline, record who made the change, when, and why, so the baseline's present content can be traced back to decisions rather than to habit. Attach the baseline change history for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Baseline change history for the period: setting changed, author, date and reason

title.en: Compare live configuration against the governing baseline and record every deviation

description.en: Establish what values the instances a baseline governs actually hold, and where those differ from the required ones. State the coverage the comparison achieved — every instance, or a named sample and how it was chosen. Record against each deviation whether it was corrected or entered as an approved exception with an owner and either the date it is to be revisited or the reason it stands indefinitely. Attach the deviation record and the exception register.

evidenceHint.en: Deviation record stating the coverage achieved, plus the exception register carrying an owner and either a revisit date or a stated reason for standing indefinitely

title.en: Re-examine each baseline against the source its values came from and record what changed

description.en: Return to the source named against each required value — external guidance or the organisation's own recorded decision — and identify values that have moved, settings newly recommended and settings no longer relevant, updating the baseline accordingly. Attach the review record naming, for each baseline, the source consulted and the version or date of the decision it stands on, together with each required value that changed as a result.

evidenceHint.en: Baseline review record naming the source consulted for each baseline and each required value changed as a result

templates.title: Information deletion
templates.description: Delete information when no longer needed

title.en: Record what makes each category of information due for deletion and where that due date is fixed

description.en: For each category of information the organisation holds, record the event that makes it due for deletion — a retention period expiring, a contract or an account ending, a request from the person it concerns, a project closing — and name where that due date is fixed, whether in a retention schedule the organisation already maintains, a statutory period or a contract term. Take the periods as given rather than setting them here. Where a category is never due for deletion, enter it with the reason. Attach the list, one row per category, as the list the holdings and the deletions are worked from.

evidenceHint.en: List of information categories, the event that makes each due for deletion, and the schedule, statute or contract that fixes it

title.en: List every place a copy of each information category is held

description.en: For each category on the retention schedule, record the systems, archives, offline media, printed files and other organisations holding a copy, with the person accountable for each holding. A deletion that misses a holding leaves the information in existence, so this list is what later makes a deletion provable. Attach the holdings list cross-referenced to the retention schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Holdings list per information category, naming each system, archive, medium or third party and its accountable owner

title.en: Record how information is removed at each holding and who performs it

description.en: For every holding on the list, state the method used to put the information beyond recovery there and the role that carries it out. Where a holding cannot delete on request — an archive written once, a copy under legal hold — record that, the date the copy expires, and the restriction applied to it meanwhile. Attach the method-per-holding table.

evidenceHint.en: Table of holding, removal method, accountable role, and the handling recorded for holdings that cannot delete on request

title.en: Carry out the deletions that fell due and show every recorded holding was cleared

description.en: Work the list for categories whose deletion event has occurred, clear them, and then set each deletion against the holdings list for its category, marking every system, archive, medium and third party as cleared, still outstanding, or unable to be cleared with the reason and the restriction standing in its place meanwhile. What this produces is a coverage sheet against the holdings list rather than a second record of the disposals themselves: where the organisation already logs a disposal elsewhere, reference that entry rather than repeating it. Attach the deletion coverage record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Deletion coverage record for the period: each deletion carried out set against every holding recorded for its category, marked cleared, outstanding or unable, with the reason for each exception

title.en: Obtain confirmation of deletion from each other organisation holding the information

description.en: For every third party on the holdings list carrying information that fell due this period, request written confirmation that it has been removed from their systems and their own copies, and record when the request was made. Attach the confirmations or destruction certificates received, together with the parties that did not answer and the follow-up taken on each.

evidenceHint.en: Third-party deletion confirmations or destruction certificates, plus the non-responder list and the follow-up on each

title.en: Search for surviving copies of a sample of information already recorded as deleted

description.en: Take a sample of entries from the deletion record and look for that information in every holding its category lists, including archives and copies held elsewhere. Record what was searched, what was found and how any surviving copy was dealt with. Attach the verification record.

evidenceHint.en: Verification record: items sampled, holdings searched, surviving copies found and how each was resolved

templates.title: Data masking
templates.description: Mask data per access control policy

title.en: List the data items whose real values must be hidden from some of the people who use them

description.en: Working from the organisation's access decisions and its obligations over personal and other regulated data, name the specific items — identifiers, contact details, financial values, health data — that must not show their real value to everyone who legitimately uses the record, and the user populations entitled to see them in full. Attach the register giving, per item, the obligation behind it and the entitled populations.

evidenceHint.en: Register of restricted items with the obligation behind each and the user populations entitled to the real value

title.en: Record how each listed item is obscured and whether the real value can be recovered

description.en: For each item in the register state what a non-entitled user sees instead — nothing, part of the value, a substitute, an aggregate — whether the real value can be recovered from what is shown, and who holds the means to recover it. Attach the register extended with the treatment, its reversibility and the holder of the recovery means.

evidenceHint.en: Register showing, per item, what is presented instead of the real value, whether it is reversible and who can reverse it

title.en: Apply the recorded treatment everywhere a listed item is shown or handed out in day-to-day use

description.en: Work through the screens, reports, printed output, extracts and interfaces to other parties where each item appears in normal operation, and make each of them present the item as the register requires. Attach, for each of those points, a sample of its output showing the item as a non-entitled user actually receives it.

evidenceHint.en: Sample output from each screen, report, extract or interface showing the item as a non-entitled user receives it

title.en: Record each occasion a person is given the real value of a listed item

description.en: Whenever someone outside the entitled population is shown or sent an unobscured value — for an investigation, a support case, a legal request — record the item, who asked, the reason given, who agreed and how long the access lasted. Attach the record covering the period, including requests that were refused.

evidenceHint.en: Record for the period of every disclosure of a real value: item, requester, reason, approver, duration, and refusals

title.en: Establish what a non-entitled user can actually obtain of a sample of listed items

description.en: Take items from the register and, using access that belongs to a population not entitled to the real value, try to obtain that value by the means genuinely available to such a user — searching or filtering on it, exporting or building a report, calling an interface, or asking a system that receives a copy. Record for each attempt what came back and whether the real value, or enough of it to reconstruct the value, was obtainable. Confirm in the same pass that the means of recovering a real value is still held only by the people the register names. Raise a fix with an owner for every attempt that succeeded. Attach the results.

evidenceHint.en: Results per item attempted: the access used, what came back, whether the real value was obtainable, and the fix raised where it was

title.en: Record the information that must not leave uncontrolled and what may happen when it does leave

description.en: Name the categories of information whose unauthorised disclosure would harm the organisation or breach an obligation, and state for each what may happen when it leaves: it must not leave at all, it may leave only with a named person's agreement, it may leave but what passes must be recorded or examined, or it may leave unrestricted with the exposure accepted. Name who agreed the position for each category. Take the organisation's transfer routes as already listed elsewhere and do not enumerate them again here. Attach the table, one row per category.

evidenceHint.en: Table of information categories, the departure allowed for each — not at all, on agreement, recorded or examined, or unrestricted — and who agreed it

title.en: Record the measure standing in front of each route that is in scope

description.en: For every in-scope route state which applies: the route is closed altogether, it is open only with a named person's agreement, it is open but what passes is recorded or examined, or it is open unrestricted with the exposure accepted. Name the owner of each measure and, for anything left unrestricted, who accepted it. Attach the route-to-measure register.

evidenceHint.en: Route-to-measure register: route, the measure in force, its owner, and the named acceptance of any route left unrestricted

title.en: Issue the handling instruction telling people the sanctioned way to send each kind of identified information

description.en: Turn the register into an instruction the people who handle this information can act on: for each closed or controlled route, the sanctioned alternative and who to ask when there is none. Attach the issued instruction with its date and the list of people or groups it was sent to.

evidenceHint.en: The issued handling instruction, its date, and the distribution list showing who received it

title.en: Record each new way information could leave that appeared this period and the measure decided for it

description.en: As a new service, device type, connection or working arrangement comes into use that gives information a further way out of the organisation, record what it is, who noticed it, which categories it could carry, and the measure decided for it — closed, allowed only under a condition, watched, or accepted — together with who decided. Where nothing new appeared in the period, record that. Attach the additions made to the route-to-measure register during the period.

evidenceHint.en: Additions to the route-to-measure register for the period: the new way out, who noticed it, the categories it could carry, the measure decided and the decider, or a statement that none appeared

title.en: Record each suspected leakage raised this period and what was done about it

description.en: Take every case that came to notice however it arrived — a person reporting a mistake, something found in an examination of a controlled route, a recipient or supplier telling the organisation, a routine check — and record what was suspected, what was established, the action taken and any change made to the route measures. Attach the record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Record for the period: each suspected leakage, how it came to notice, what was established, the action taken and any change to the measures

title.en: Test each measure in force against uncontrolled departure and record whether it behaved as recorded

description.en: Take the measures on the route-to-measure register one at a time and establish what each actually does with harmless data of the identified kind: for a measure recorded as closing a way out, attempt to use it; for one that requires an agreement, attempt without the agreement; for one that records or examines what passes, send something and then look for it in what was recorded; for anything left accepted, confirm the acceptance is still held by the person named. Record the result against each measure and the correction made wherever the behaviour did not match the register. Attach the results.

evidenceHint.en: Results per measure in force: what was attempted against it, what it did, and the correction made where the behaviour did not match the register

title.en: Register the systems and datasets in backup scope with their required frequency and retention

description.en: List what must be backed up, how often each item needs a copy taken, and how long copies are kept, derived from the business need for that data. Attach the backup scope register showing system, dataset, frequency and retention.

title.en: Configure the backup jobs to the registered schedule, including a copy held separately

description.en: Set up jobs covering every entry in the register, with at least one copy kept in a separate location or account so a failure at the primary site does not take the backups with it. Attach the job configuration export mapped line by line to the register.

title.en: Apply encryption and access restriction to the backup copies

description.en: Encrypt backup data at rest and in transit and limit who can read, alter or delete the backup repository, recording where the keys are held. Attach the encryption and access-control configuration for the backup repository, with the list of accounts holding delete rights.

title.en: Review the backup job outcomes for this period and resolve every failure

description.en: Check the completion status of each scheduled job, investigate failed and partial runs, and record the fix or the re-run. Attach the job status report for the period showing each job's result and the resolution of any failure.

evidenceHint.en: Backup job status report for the period, with the resolution recorded per failure

title.en: Restore data from backup and record what came back and how long it took

description.en: Perform an actual restore into an isolated environment, verify the restored data is complete and usable, and note the elapsed time. Attach the restore test record naming the backup set used, the data verified and the duration — a job that reports success is not proof the data is recoverable.

evidenceHint.en: Restore test record: backup set restored, verification performed, elapsed time

title.en: Reconcile the configured backup jobs against the systems inventory to expose unprotected systems

description.en: Compare the systems actually covered by a running job against the full systems inventory, and list every system with no backup. Attach the reconciliation with each gap and the decision taken — add a job, or record why the system needs none.

title.en: Record the availability requirement for each information processing facility in scope

description.en: For every service or facility the business depends on, state the availability it must sustain and the maximum tolerable outage, agreed with the service owner. Attach the service list with those targets — redundancy decisions are only assessable against a stated requirement.

title.en: Identify the single points of failure in each in-scope service's architecture

description.en: Walk each service's components — compute, storage, network path, power, supplier dependency — and mark every element whose loss would stop the service. Attach the analysis per service listing the single points of failure found.

title.en: Provision the redundant component for each single point of failure being addressed

description.en: Put the duplicate component, alternate path or standby facility in place for the failure points the availability requirement demands, and record the ones deliberately left unaddressed with the reason. Attach the architecture record showing the redundant path per service.

title.en: Fail over to the redundant component and record the switchover result

description.en: Take the primary component out of service under controlled conditions, confirm the service continues on the redundant one, and record the time taken to switch and anything that did not carry over. Attach the failover test record per service tested.

evidenceHint.en: Failover test record: service, component failed over, switchover time, issues found

title.en: Compare measured availability against the recorded requirement for each service

description.en: Pull the actual uptime and outage duration for the period and set it beside each service's stated target, identifying every service that fell short and why. Attach the availability report with the shortfalls and the remedial action agreed.

title.en: Record the events each system must produce a record of, and where those records go

description.en: Go through the systems in use and decide, per system, which classes of event are recorded — sign-in and sign-in failure, use of elevated rights, access to held information, configuration change, error and failure. Where a system produces no record, enter it with the reason rather than omitting it. Attach the logging register, one row per system with its event classes and the destination the records are kept in.

evidenceHint.en: Logging register: system, event classes recorded, destination, and the systems recording nothing with the reason

title.en: Record where each source's records are kept and for how long

description.en: For every source in the register, record the place the records are held, the form they are held in, and how long they are kept before disposal — stated per event class where the periods differ. Attach the register extended with the holding place, form and retention for every source.

evidenceHint.en: Logging register extended with the holding place, form and retention period for every source

title.en: Reduce the set of people able to alter or remove stored records to a named minimum

description.en: For each holding place, establish who can change or delete a record once it is stored and cut that to the smallest named set, kept separate from the people who administer the systems the records come from. Attach, per holding place, the list of who retains that ability with the reason each is on it.

evidenceHint.en: Per holding place, the named list of people able to alter or remove stored records, with the reason each retains it

title.en: Confirm every source in the register is still producing records and raise the gaps

description.en: For each source, find the most recent record it produced and compare that against how often the source is expected to produce one. Raise every source silent beyond its expected interval with the person accountable for it, by whatever route the organisation uses to pursue such things, and record what the investigation found. Attach the check covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Delivery check for the period: source, most recent record, the gaps raised and the outcome of each

title.en: Attempt to alter and to remove a stored record using an ordinary administrator's access

description.en: With the owner's agreement, use an account that administers a logged system to try first to change and then to delete one of that system's stored records, and record exactly what the holding place did in each case. Attach the test record naming the access used, the attempts made, the result of each, and any restriction changed afterwards.

evidenceHint.en: Test record: the access used, the attempts made, the result of each, and the restriction changed as a result

title.en: Record which systems and networks are watched and the behaviour each is watched for

description.en: For every watched target, name the behaviour that would matter — repeated failed sign-ins, access at an unusual hour, an unexpected outbound connection, rights being raised, a service stopping — and the record or signal that behaviour would show up in. A target entered simply as 'monitored' says nothing; the behaviour is the entry. Attach the watch list.

evidenceHint.en: Watch list: target, the behaviours watched for, and the record or signal each would be recognised from

title.en: Record how each listed behaviour is looked for and how often

description.en: For every row of the watch list, say whether the behaviour is looked for continuously, at a stated interval by a named person reading the records, or in a report produced on a schedule — and who does the looking. Where a behaviour is not looked for at all today, record it as a gap rather than leaving the row blank. Attach the watch list extended with method, interval and person, plus the gap list.

evidenceHint.en: Watch list extended with how, how often and by whom each behaviour is looked for, plus the behaviours with no method yet

title.en: Name who is told when a listed behaviour is seen and what they do first

description.en: For each behaviour, name the team or rota that is told, the way word reaches them, the first action expected of them — investigate, escalate, or set aside with a stated reason — and who it passes to if they do not act. Attach the routing table covering every row of the watch list.

evidenceHint.en: Routing table: behaviour, who is told, how word reaches them, the first action expected, and the escalation

title.en: Record every observation of a watched behaviour in the period and its disposition

description.en: Take the observations that arose, however they arose, and record for each what was seen, when, who dealt with it, whether it turned out to be genuine, mistaken or already known, what was done in response, and any change made to the watch list as a result. Attach the observation record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Observation record for the period: what was seen, when, who dealt with it, the disposition, the action taken and any change to the watch list

title.en: Produce a watched behaviour deliberately and record whether it was noticed

description.en: Choose a behaviour from the watch list, arrange with the target's owner to produce it at a known time, then record whether it was noticed, how long afterwards, by whom, and whether the person named to be told actually heard. Where it went unnoticed, record what was changed. Attach the exercise record.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise record: behaviour produced, time produced, whether and when it was noticed, by whom, who was told, and the correction made

title.en: List every system that records timestamps and the time source it currently uses

description.en: Go through the systems inventory — servers, network devices, workstations, appliances and hosted services — and record for each the time source it is presently configured against and the offset measured at the time of the check. Attach the clock inventory with a row per system.

evidenceHint.en: Clock inventory: system, current configured time source, measured offset at the time of the check.

title.en: Record the approved time source and the tolerated drift in a written standard

description.en: Name the primary and fallback time source, the protocol used to reach them, and the maximum offset a system may show before it is treated as a fault. State which system classes the standard covers and how a system without direct reachability to the source is served. Attach the standard.

evidenceHint.en: Written time standard naming the primary and fallback source, the protocol and the maximum tolerated offset.

title.en: Point each system in the clock inventory at the approved time source

description.en: Reconfigure every system whose recorded source is not the approved one, working through the inventory, and record the systems that cannot be changed together with the reason and the arrangement covering them. Attach the per-system configuration output showing the source in effect after the change.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system configuration output after the change, plus the list of systems that could not be repointed and why.

title.en: Measure the clock offset of each system against the approved source

description.en: Run the offset check across the inventory, record the reading for every system, and raise the systems exceeding the tolerated drift for correction, noting what was done. Attach the offset readings for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Offset readings for the period, one per system, with systems outside tolerance flagged and the correction recorded.

title.en: Trace one event across the logs of two systems and compare the recorded timestamps

description.en: Choose an event both systems record — a sign-in crossing an authentication service and an application, for instance — extract the timestamp each wrote, and compare the difference against the tolerated drift in the standard. Attach the correlated trace showing both log entries, the difference, and any follow-up raised.

evidenceHint.en: Correlated event trace with both systems' log entries, the timestamp difference and the follow-up raised.

title.en: List the programs able to override a system or application control, and where they are installed

description.en: Go through the builds in service for tools that can bypass an access check, write directly to storage or memory, read or reset credentials, or change what is recorded. Record each one with the systems it is present on and the specific control it is able to override. Attach the inventory.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory: program, the systems it is present on, and the control it is able to override

title.en: Record who may run each listed program, on which systems, and in what circumstance

description.en: For every entry in the inventory, name the role permitted to run it, the systems that permission covers, and the circumstance that justifies a run — a recovery, an examination, a migration. Where no role needs it, mark the entry for removal rather than leaving it unassigned. Attach the permission record.

evidenceHint.en: Permission record: program, permitted role, the systems covered, and the circumstance that justifies a run

title.en: Remove or place beyond ordinary reach every listed program with no permitted user

description.en: On each system holding an entry marked for removal, take the program off; where it cannot be taken off because the platform supplies it, restrict who is able to invoke it. Where neither is possible, record the restriction standing in its place and who accepted the residual exposure. Attach the state of each affected system before and after.

evidenceHint.en: Per system, the state before and after: the program removed, its invocation restricted, or the accepted compensating restriction

title.en: Record each run of a listed program with the person, the system and the reason

description.en: Capture every occasion one of the inventoried programs is used, taking it from whatever records the run — the system's own records, an operator's entry in a register, the request that authorised it — so the run is attributable to a person and a purpose rather than only to an account. Attach the record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Record for the period: program, person, system, date, and the stated reason for the run

title.en: Account for every recorded run that the permission record does not cover

description.en: Compare each run recorded in the period against the role, system and circumstance the permission record allows, and list the runs with no match. Record what investigating each one found and how it ended — the permission widened, the access withdrawn, or an incident raised. Attach the comparison.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of recorded runs against the permission record, listing the unmatched runs and how each was resolved

templates.title: Installation of software on operational systems

title.en: Record what says whether a piece of software belongs on each class of operational system

description.en: For every class of system in service — a server role, a standard workstation build, an appliance — record what determines whether a piece of software belongs there: an enumerated list of permitted software with versions where the version matters, a managed image or repository whose contents can be produced on request, or the record of approvals and installations for that class. Name the person accountable for keeping it current. Attach whichever of these the organisation holds, one per class.

evidenceHint.en: Per system class, what says whether software belongs there — a permitted list, a managed image or repository contents, or the recorded approvals — with the accountable owner of each

title.en: Write down who may install software on an operational system and what must happen first

description.en: State which roles may install, what approval a package must carry before it may be installed at all, what must be recorded at the time of installing, and how the version being replaced is kept available so an installation can be undone. Where the organisation maintains a permitted list, say how an approved package reaches it; where it does not, the recorded approval stands as the authority on its own. Attach the written rule showing who approved it and when.

evidenceHint.en: The written installation rule naming the permitted roles, the approval a package must carry, what is recorded at installation, and how an installation is undone

title.en: Reduce the ability to install software on operational systems to the people the rule permits

description.en: Work class by class, taking the ability to install away from anyone the rule does not name. Where it cannot be taken away — a platform where operating it is inseparable from installing on it — record the system, the reason, and what stands in place of the restriction. Attach, per class, the list of who retains the ability.

evidenceHint.en: Per system class, who retains the ability to install software, plus the systems where it could not be reduced and what compensates

title.en: Record every installation and version change made on an operational system this period

description.en: For each one, record the system, the software, the version put on and the version it replaced, who did it, and the approval it was carried out under. Where installing is done by hand, make the entry at the time rather than reconstructing it afterwards. Attach the installation record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Installation record for the period: system, software, version installed and the version replaced, installer, and the approval reference

title.en: Account for software found on a sample of operational systems that nothing recorded explains

description.en: Take a sample spanning the system classes, list what is actually present on each, and set that against the reference state recorded for the class and the installation record. For every item neither explains, record what it is, how it arrived if that can be established, and the decision taken — removed, or approved and brought within the reference state. Attach the findings.

evidenceHint.en: Findings from the sampled systems: the unexplained software found, what was established about it, and the decision on each

title.en: List the networks the organisation operates and name who is accountable for each

description.en: Record every network in use — office, data centre, cloud virtual network, wireless, remote access, and any network serving visitors or equipment rather than staff — with what it carries, who uses it, and the named person accountable for it.
