Attach the network register with a row per network.

evidenceHint.en: Network register: network, what it carries, who uses it, and the named person accountable for it

title.en: Record every point at which a registered network meets something outside the organisation's control

description.en: For each registered network, list the links to anything the organisation does not itself run — internet access, provider circuits, partner connections, remote access into it, wireless reaching beyond the premises — with the purpose of each and the person who authorised it. A link nobody can account for is the finding this task exists to surface. Attach the external-connection register.

evidenceHint.en: External-connection register: network, the connection, its purpose, and who authorised it

title.en: Record the protection required for the organisation's information as it crosses each of those connections

description.en: For every connection on the register, state what must be protected while it is in transit and to what standard, and name the traffic that crosses unprotected together with the reason it is accepted and who accepted it. Attach the register extended with the protection required per connection.

evidenceHint.en: External-connection register extended with the in-transit protection required, including traffic accepted as unprotected and who accepted it

title.en: Account for what is attached to each registered network this period

description.en: Establish what is currently present on each registered network, by whatever means that network yields, and set it against what is expected there. Record every device, service or connection found that no record explains, what it turned out to be, and whether it was removed, moved or recorded as legitimate. Attach the findings for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Findings per network for the period: what was found attached, the items no record explained, and the outcome for each

title.en: Reconfirm that each recorded external connection is still needed and still protected as recorded

description.en: Walk the external-connection register with the person accountable for each network: confirm the purpose still holds, that the protection actually in place is the protection recorded, and withdraw the connections no longer needed. Record the decision taken on every entry, including those removed. Attach the reconfirmation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconfirmation of the register: per connection, whether still needed, whether the protection matches the record, and the decision taken

templates.title: Security of network services
templates.description: Address security in network service agreements

title.en: List the network services in use and the provider of each

description.en: Record every network service the organisation consumes, internally provided and externally purchased — internet access, wide-area links, DNS, VPN, cloud connectivity, wireless — with its business use, the provider, and the contract or internal service description that governs it. Attach the network service register.

evidenceHint.en: Network service register: service, provider, business use and the governing agreement reference.

title.en: Record the security mechanisms and service levels agreed for each network service

description.en: For every service in the register, extract from its contract, service level agreement or internal service description the security mechanisms committed (authentication, encryption, filtering, resilience), the availability commitment and the management arrangements. Mark services whose agreement carries no such terms as gaps. Attach the per-service record citing the clause.

evidenceHint.en: Per-service record of agreed security mechanisms, service levels and management arrangements, citing the clause, with the gap list.

title.en: Record the assurance the organisation may obtain for each externally provided network service

description.en: For each external service, note what its agreement entitles the organisation to — audit, an assurance or certification report, service reporting — and where the most recent evidence received is filed. Mark services entitling the organisation to nothing so the exposure is visible. Attach the assurance column of the register with clause references.

evidenceHint.en: Assurance entries per external service: the clause relied on, the assurance type, and the location and date of the latest evidence received.

title.en: Record delivered service levels and provider incidents for each network service in the period

description.en: Collect provider reporting or internal measurement for every service, note where delivery fell short of the agreed levels, and record any incident raised with the provider and the response given. Attach the service performance record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Service performance record for the period per network service, with shortfalls against agreed levels, incidents raised and provider responses.

title.en: Check each network service in use against its agreement for the mechanisms actually in place

description.en: Taking one service at a time, confirm the mechanisms its agreement names are configured and working — encryption enabled, filtering active, resilient path exercised — and identify services in use with no agreement at all. Attach the comparison listing findings, the service owner and the remediation owner for each.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of agreed mechanisms against those in place per service, listing findings, services with no agreement, and the remediation owner.

title.en: Record the network domains in use and why each is held apart

description.en: Work with the people who run the network to list each domain in use — grouped by trust level, by business function, or by the sensitivity of what it carries — and for each record the systems and user groups that sit in it and the reason it is kept apart from the others. Mark any system not yet assigned to a domain. Attach the dated domain list.

evidenceHint.en: The domain list: each domain, its systems and users, and the reason it is separated

title.en: Record what may pass between each pair of domains and who authorised it

description.en: Build a permitted-flow list holding one row per connection allowed to cross a domain boundary: source domain, destination domain, what the connection carries, the business reason, and the person who authorised it. State on the list that anything not held on it is not permitted, and cross-reference every row to the domain list. Attach the permitted-flow list.

evidenceHint.en: The permitted-flow list, one row per allowed cross-domain connection with its authoriser

title.en: Record how the permitted-flow list is enforced at each boundary

description.en: For each pair of domains, record the measure that actually holds the boundary — whatever the organisation uses, from separate physical infrastructure to filtering at a shared gateway — the team that maintains it, and how a connection absent from the permitted-flow list is prevented. Remove, or raise for decision, anything found in place that no row on the list justifies. Attach the boundary record cross-referenced to the list, showing the disposal of each unjustified item.

evidenceHint.en: Boundary record naming the enforcement measure and maintainer per domain pair, with unjustified items dispositioned

title.en: Record every change to what is permitted between domains

description.en: For each row added to, amended on, or removed from the permitted-flow list during the period, capture who asked for it, what changed, the reason and the date it took effect, using the record the network team already keeps rather than a second one. Attach the change record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Change record for the period, one entry per permitted-flow row added, amended or removed

title.en: Test what can actually be reached from each domain against the permitted-flow list

description.en: From a position inside each domain, attempt to reach destinations in the other domains, covering both connections the list permits and a sample it does not, and record the observed outcome for every attempt. Raise remediation with a named owner wherever observation and list disagree. Attach the results with the disagreements and their remediation.

evidenceHint.en: Reachability results, one row per source and destination attempted, with disagreements and remediation

title.en: Record which external web content must not be reachable, and by whom

description.en: For each group of users and devices — staff, contractors, shared or public-facing machines, servers — state what kinds of external site are not to be reachable, what is allowed, and how something fitting none of the stated kinds is treated. Name the person who agreed the position for each group. Attach the position table.

evidenceHint.en: The position table: one row per kind of content showing the outcome for each user and device group

title.en: Record how the position is achieved for each group, and what it covers

description.en: For each group in the position table, record the arrangement that carries the restriction, the point at which it takes effect, and who maintains it. List the devices and connections covered by it and, separately, those that are not covered together with what is done about them. Attach the coverage record.

evidenceHint.en: Coverage record naming the arrangement per group and listing covered and uncovered devices

title.en: Record and publish the route by which access to restricted content is asked for and decided

description.en: Write down where such a request is raised — which may be the organisation's existing change or service route — what the requester must supply, who decides, and where the decision is recorded. Make it reachable by the people the restriction affects and attach evidence of how they reach it, whether that is the point at which access is refused, an internal page, the service route itself, or an instruction issued to the group. Attach the published text.

evidenceHint.en: The recorded request route and evidence of how the affected users reach it

title.en: Record each access allowed through the restriction, with its scope and the point at which it is revisited

description.en: Keep one register entry per access allowed through: what was allowed, for whom, the reason given, who decided, and either the date the access ends or, where the need is standing, the point at which it is to be revisited. Close entries as they end and record the outcome when a standing entry is revisited, so the register shows what is open today and on what basis. Where the restriction admits no exceptions for a group, record that rather than keeping an empty register. Attach the register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Register of access allowed through for the period: scope, requester, reason, decider, and an end date or stated revisit point, with closed and revisited entries shown

title.en: Attempt a representative site from each restricted kind and record what happened

description.en: From a device in each covered group, try to reach one representative site for every kind of content the position table says must not be reachable, and record the outcome of each attempt. Raise a fix, with an owner, wherever access succeeded that should not have. Attach the attempt sheet.

evidenceHint.en: Attempt sheet: site, kind, user group and observed outcome, with fixes raised

title.en: Inventory every system and application using cryptography

description.en: Walk the system inventory with the teams that run each system and record where cryptography is used — data at rest, data in transit, signing, tokens — naming the system, the algorithm and the purpose of each use.

evidenceHint.en: The cryptography inventory, listing system, algorithm and purpose for every use.

title.en: Record the approved algorithms and minimum key lengths for each use

description.en: For each use case in the inventory (transport, storage, signing, hashing, password storage), write down which algorithms are approved, the minimum key length or parameter set, and which are no longer permitted.

evidenceHint.en: The cryptographic standard, showing approved algorithm and minimum key length per use case.

title.en: Record how each key is generated, distributed, rotated and destroyed

description.en: Build a key register with one row per key or key set, covering where it is generated, who holds it, how it reaches the systems that need it, its rotation interval, and how it is destroyed at end of life.

evidenceHint.en: The key register, one row per key with generation, custody, rotation interval and destruction method.

title.en: Log every key generation, rotation, revocation and destruction

description.en: Capture each key lifecycle event as it happens — which key, which event, who performed it and when — so that what the register claims can be proven against real activity.

evidenceHint.en: The key-management log for the period, one entry per lifecycle event.

title.en: Reconcile the key register against the cryptography inventory

description.en: Compare the register with the systems inventory, listing keys in live use that have no register row and register rows for keys no longer in use, and record how each discrepancy was resolved.

evidenceHint.en: The reconciliation, with every discrepancy found and its resolution.

title.en: Record the development work the lifecycle governs and who performs each kind

description.en: State the kinds of work in scope — new systems, changes to systems already in use, configuration of software the organisation acquired, and work carried out by suppliers on its behalf — and who performs each. Mark anything deliberately outside the lifecycle together with the reason it is excluded. Attach the scope statement.

evidenceHint.en: Scope statement naming each kind of development work, who performs it, and the reason for any exclusion

title.en: Write the lifecycle stages and the security output each stage must produce

description.en: Set out the stages a piece of development passes through and, for each, the security output that must exist before the stage is complete and where that output is held. Name the outputs as deliverables rather than as tools, so a team working on paper and a team working in a toolchain can both satisfy them. Attach the lifecycle definition.

evidenceHint.en: The lifecycle definition: each stage, the security output required, and where that output is held

title.en: Record who confirms each stage is complete and how a stage may be waived

description.en: Name the person or role accountable for confirming each stage's output exists before the next stage begins, then write down the authority needed to waive a stage, what must be recorded when one is waived, and how long a waiver stands. Attach the accountability list and the written waiver route.

evidenceHint.en: Accountability list per stage plus the written waiver route and the authority it names

title.en: Record the lifecycle stages completed for each product released this period

description.en: For every release in the period, capture which stages were completed, where each stage's output is held, and any stage waived with the authority for it, inside the release record the team already produces. Attach the release records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Release records for the period, each naming the stages completed, their outputs and any waiver

title.en: Sample completed development work and check it stage by stage against the lifecycle

description.en: Take a sample of work finished in the period, walk each item through the lifecycle definition, and record for every stage whether the required output exists. Raise each missing output with the person named for that stage on the accountability list. Attach the review with its gaps and owners.

evidenceHint.en: The sampled review, one row per item and stage, with missing outputs and their owners

templates.title: Application security requirements
templates.description: Identify and address application security needs

title.en: List the applications needing a security requirement set, with what each handles

description.en: Record the applications the organisation builds, buys or subscribes to, noting for each the owner, the information it handles, who can reach it, and whether it exchanges information across networks the organisation does not control. Mark which of them need a documented security requirement set. Attach the application list.

evidenceHint.en: Application list with owner, information handled, reachability, and the requirement-set decision per entry

title.en: Write the standing security requirements every application must meet

description.en: State as requirements, not as products, what any application must do: how it establishes who a user is and what they may do, how it handles information held and in transit, what it records about significant actions, how it behaves on invalid input and on failure, and what integrity a transaction it carries must retain. Attach the approved standing requirement set with its approver and date.

evidenceHint.en: The approved standing security requirement set, with approver and date

title.en: Derive and record the security requirements for each application in scope

description.en: For every application marked in scope, record which standing requirements apply, which do not and why, and what further requirements its information and reachability demand. Hold the result where the delivery or procurement work for that application is already tracked, linked to its list entry. Attach the requirement set for each in-scope application.

evidenceHint.en: Per-application requirement sets, each linked to its application list entry

title.en: Record the security requirements set for each application acquired or newly specified

description.en: As each application is specified or bought in the period, capture the security requirements it was required to meet, who agreed them with the business owner, and what was offered as evidence that the application meets them. Attach the record for each acquisition or specification in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Per-acquisition record naming the requirements set, who agreed them, and the evidence offered

title.en: Re-examine the standing requirements against what has changed

description.en: Review the standing requirement set against new obligations, new kinds of exposure, and the defects and incidents seen since it was written, recording what was added, amended or dropped and why. List the applications whose own requirement sets must now be brought up to it, with an owner each. Attach the revised set and the catch-up list.

evidenceHint.en: The revised standing requirement set plus the list of applications to be brought up to it

templates.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles

title.en: Write down the engineering principles systems are designed to

description.en: Agree the principles the organisation designs to and give each one line saying what it means for our systems rather than in the abstract. Record who approved the set and when. Attach the principles document.

evidenceHint.en: The approved principles document, one entry per principle with its meaning here

title.en: Record how the principles are met in one existing design, as the worked example

description.en: Take one system the organisation runs, describe its parts, the boundaries between them and where trust changes, and annotate each with the principle it satisfies and how. Where the system does not satisfy a principle, say so on the same document rather than omitting it. Attach the annotated design as the example other designs are shaped against.

evidenceHint.en: The annotated design of one real system showing which principle each part satisfies

title.en: Record when a design is examined against the principles and how a departure is authorised

description.en: State at what point in the work a design must be examined, what the examiner looks at, who may accept a departure from a principle, and where the outcome is recorded. Produce the form or record layout the examination fills in. Attach the written arrangement and the blank record.

evidenceHint.en: The written examination arrangement plus the blank examination record

title.en: Record the examination outcome for each system designed or substantially redesigned

description.en: For every design examined in the period, capture which principles it was examined against, what was found, and any departure accepted together with the person who accepted it and the reason given. Attach the completed examination records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Completed examination records for the period, naming principles checked and departures accepted

title.en: Check that every system designed or redesigned in the period was examined, and what the departures say about the principles

description.en: List the systems designed or substantially redesigned in the period from wherever that work is tracked, and set that list against the examination records held for the period. Record every one that was not examined, why it was missed, and the owner who will close it. Then read the departures accepted across those examinations together: where the same principle is departed from repeatedly, record whether it is to be restated, kept as it stands, or supported differently, and who decided. Attach the comparison and the conclusion drawn.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of the period's designs and redesigns against the examinations held, naming the systems missed and the conclusion drawn about repeatedly departed principles

title.en: List the languages, frameworks and code in use and the coding rules that apply to each

description.en: Record every language and framework the organisation writes in, including scripts and infrastructure definitions, and name the secure coding rules that apply to each. Flag any for which no rules have been chosen yet. Attach the list with the rules cited or the gap flagged per row.

evidenceHint.en: The language and framework list, each row citing its coding rules or flagging the gap

title.en: Write the secure coding rules developers are expected to follow

description.en: Cover at least the handling of untrusted input, the construction of output, error and failure behaviour, the handling of secrets and credentials, and the use of code the organisation did not write. Publish the rules where developers already work. Attach the published rules and evidence of where developers reach them.

evidenceHint.en: The published secure coding rules and where developers reach them

title.en: Record what confirms each coding rule has been followed, and who is accountable for it

description.en: For every rule, or group of rules, record what confirms it has been followed — a person reading the code, an automated check, or both — and who is accountable for that confirmation. Where a confirmation is a test that already sits on the organisation's security testing schedule, name it by reference rather than restating what it does or when it runs. Where a rule has no check at all, record it as unchecked rather than leaving it unstated. Attach the rule-to-check map.

evidenceHint.en: Rule-to-check map naming the confirming person or check for every rule, with unchecked rules shown as such

title.en: Record, for each change accepted this period, which rule confirmations were completed and by whom

description.en: For every change accepted into the codebase in the period, capture which of the confirmations named on the rule-to-check map were completed for it and who or what completed each — the person who read the code where a person is the confirmer, the check that ran where it is not — taken from the record the team already produces when accepting code rather than re-keyed into a new one. Record which rules the code was read against, and leave the completion and result of the scheduled security tests to be filed against the change under the testing arrangement rather than repeating them here. Attach the acceptance records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Acceptance records for the period showing, per change, the rule confirmations completed and the person or check that completed each

title.en: Read a sample of accepted code against the rules by hand

description.en: Take a sample of changes accepted in the period and read the code against the written rules, done by someone other than whoever accepted it. Record each finding with the rule it breaches, the fix raised and the owner of that fix. Attach the sample review record.

evidenceHint.en: Sample review record naming the rule breached and the fix raised for each finding

templates.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
templates.description: Test security during development and acceptance

title.en: Record the security tests each kind of change must pass and what each covers

description.en: List the security tests in use and, for each, state what it examines, what part of the system it covers, and which kinds of change must pass it before being accepted. Mark any kind of change that requires no test together with the reason. Attach the test schedule.

evidenceHint.en: The test schedule: each test, what it covers, and the kinds of change that must pass it

title.en: Record the result each test must reach for a change to be accepted

description.en: For every test on the schedule, state the outcome that permits acceptance, what counts as a failure, and who may accept a change whose result falls short and on what record. Agree the thresholds with the person accountable for putting changes into use. Attach the acceptance criteria and the shortfall route.

evidenceHint.en: Acceptance criteria per test, with the named authority for accepting a shortfall

title.en: File the security test results that supported each acceptance decision

description.en: For every change accepted in the period, capture the result of each test the schedule required for it and hold that result against the record of the change, so the acceptance decision can be judged from it afterwards. Attach the results filed for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Test results filed against each accepted change for the period

title.en: Record a disposition and an owner for every finding the testing raised

description.en: Work through the findings raised by testing in the period and record for each whether it is to be fixed, accepted as it stands, or set aside as not a real finding, naming the person who decided, the owner and the date. Leave no finding without a disposition. Attach the findings record.

evidenceHint.en: Findings record for the period, each finding carrying a disposition, decider and owner

title.en: Sample changes put into use and confirm the required tests were passed

description.en: Take a sample of changes put into use in the period and trace each back to the tests the schedule required for it, checking that the results met the acceptance criteria or carried a recorded shortfall acceptance. Record every change that went in without them, with an owner. Attach the sample review.

evidenceHint.en: Sample review listing the changes checked and any accepted without the required results

title.en: Register every supplier performing development work for the organisation

description.en: Identify the external parties writing, extending or maintaining code, and record for each what they build and which systems and data their work touches. Attach the supplier register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of outsourced development suppliers with scope of work and systems touched

title.en: Record the security requirements every outsourced development contract must carry

description.en: Set out the requirements to be placed on a development supplier — secure development practice, testing obligations, code and IP ownership, vulnerability handling, and the organisation's right to review. Drafted with Legal. Attach the requirement set and the contract clauses referencing it.

evidenceHint.en: Security requirement set for development contracts, with the clauses that carry it

title.en: Define how supplier-written code enters the organisation's codebase

description.en: State the intake route for outsourced deliverables — where code is received, who reviews it, which tests it must pass, and what blocks a merge. Attach the intake procedure naming the review and testing gates.

evidenceHint.en: Intake procedure for outsourced code, naming the review and testing gates before merge

title.en: Test each outsourced deliverable for security defects before acceptance

description.en: Run the agreed review and security tests against the deliverable and record the findings raised before it is accepted and paid for. Attach the acceptance review record per deliverable.

evidenceHint.en: Acceptance review and test record for each deliverable, with findings raised

title.en: Assess each development supplier against its contracted security requirements

description.en: For every supplier on the register, check practice against the requirements the contract carries, and record gaps with a remediation owner and agreed action. Attach the assessment record per supplier.

evidenceHint.en: Per-supplier assessment record showing gaps against contracted requirements and remediation

templates.title: Separation of development, test and production environments

title.en: List the environments each system has and which of them hold live information

description.en: For every system, record the environments in use — development, test, the one carrying live operation, and any other — with the purpose of each, where it is hosted, who owns it, and whether it holds information taken from live operation. Attach the environment list.

evidenceHint.en: Environment list: system, environment, purpose, hosting, owner, and whether it holds live-derived information

title.en: Record how each environment is kept apart from live operation and who maintains that

description.en: For each environment on the list, record the measure that keeps it from reaching or affecting live operation — whatever the organisation uses, from separate hardware or separate hosting accounts through to distinct credentials and addressing — and the team that maintains it. Attach the separation record, one entry per environment.

evidenceHint.en: Separation record naming the measure and the maintaining team for each environment

title.en: Record who may work in each environment and what they may do there, and set access to match

description.en: State per environment which roles may enter it and what they may do once there, then set the entitlements held in each environment to agree with that statement and remove what does not. Where a person or an account holds entitlements in more than one environment, leave that standing only where the role statement allows it, and record it on the cross-environment register. Attach the statement together with the resulting access list per environment.

evidenceHint.en: Per-environment role statement plus the access list showing it applied, with anything spanning environments recorded on the cross-environment register

title.en: Record the route by which code and configuration reach live operation

description.en: Write down the permitted direction of travel between environments, who may move something along it, and what must already have happened before something enters live operation. State also what is to be done on the occasions when something has to be changed directly in live operation. Attach the written route.

evidenceHint.en: The written route naming the permitted direction, who may move, and the preconditions

title.en: Record each access that spans more than one environment, with its reason and end date

description.en: Whenever a person or an account is given access covering both live operation and a development or test environment, record who granted it, the reason, and the date it ends; close the entry when the access is withdrawn. Attach the register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Register of cross-environment access for the period, with reason, grantor and end date

title.en: Verify that a development or test environment cannot reach live information

description.en: From within a sample of development and test environments, attempt to reach live systems and live information by the means available there, recording what was attempted and what happened in each case. Raise remediation with an owner wherever an attempt succeeded. Attach the verification record.

evidenceHint.en: Verification record: environment, what was attempted, the outcome, and remediation raised

templates.title: Change management
templates.description: Manage changes to information processing facilities

title.en: Define which changes to information processing facilities require the change route

description.en: State the classes of change that must go through the change procedure and those that are pre-approved as standard, so it is unambiguous which route a given change takes. Attach the scope definition with the change classes and exclusions.

evidenceHint.en: Scope definition naming the change classes in and out of the change procedure

title.en: Record the change procedure from request through approval to back-out

description.en: Document each stage a change passes through — request, impact assessment, approval, testing, implementation, back-out — naming who acts at each. Attach the procedure document.

evidenceHint.en: Change procedure document covering request, assessment, approval, testing and back-out

title.en: Make impact assessment and back-out plan mandatory fields on the change record

description.en: Configure the change record or tracking tool so a change cannot be submitted for approval without an impact assessment and a stated back-out plan. Attach the record template or tool configuration showing the mandatory fields.

evidenceHint.en: Change record template or tool configuration showing the mandatory assessment and back-out fields

title.en: Record each change with its assessment, approval, test result and outcome

description.en: Keep one record per change carrying the assessment made, who approved it, the result of testing and whether implementation succeeded or was backed out. Attach the change register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Change register for the period, one row per change with assessment, approver, test result and outcome

title.en: Record the retrospective approval for every change made outside the normal route

description.en: Where a change had to be made urgently, capture what was done, who authorised it at the time, and the approval recorded afterwards. Attach the emergency change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Emergency change log with the after-the-fact approval recorded against each entry

title.en: Sample production changes and confirm approval preceded implementation

description.en: Take a sample of changes from the register and check that the recorded approval carries a date before the implementation date, listing any that do not. Attach the sample review with the exceptions found.

evidenceHint.en: Sample review listing changes checked and any implemented without prior approval

title.en: Record what information each testing activity needs and where it comes from

description.en: List the testing activities carried out and, for each, the information it needs, whether that information can be made up or must be derived from live records, and the reason live-derived information is necessary. Attach the needs list.

evidenceHint.en: Needs list: testing activity, information required, source, and the reason live-derived information is needed

title.en: Record who authorises live-derived information for testing and on what terms

description.en: Write down who may authorise a copy of live-derived information for testing, what must be done to it before it is used, where it may be held, how long it may be kept, and what happens to it when that period ends. Attach the written terms naming the authorising role.

evidenceHint.en: Written authorisation terms naming the authorising role, the holding limits and the end-of-use action

title.en: Record every test dataset already held, its origin and its removal date

description.en: Go through the environments in use and record each dataset held for testing: where it came from, whether it derives from live records, what protection it carries, who authorised it, and when it is due to be removed. Mark any dataset found with no authorisation behind it. Attach the test information register.

evidenceHint.en: Test information register, one row per dataset with origin, protection, authoriser and removal date

title.en: Record each live-derived copy taken for testing this period

description.en: For every copy made in the period, record the source, the destination environment, what was done to the information before it was used, who authorised it, and the date it falls due for removal, adding the row to the test information register. Attach the copy record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Copy record for the period, one row per copy with source, destination, authoriser and removal date

title.en: Remove the test information whose authorised holding period has ended

description.en: Work the register for entries past their removal date, remove or return the information wherever it is held, and record what was removed, from where and by whom, closing the register entry as you go. Attach the removal record for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Removal record for the period naming each dataset removed, its location and who removed it

title.en: Compare the test information actually held against the register

description.en: Inspect the environments on the list and compare what is held there with the register, reporting anything held that the register does not show, anything past its removal date, and anything held with no authorisation behind it. Raise each with a named owner. Attach the comparison with its findings.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison record listing unregistered, overdue and unauthorised test information with owners

templates.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing

title.en: Record the systems, information and actions each planned audit test will reach

description.en: Before the test begins, and with the person who will carry it out, record which systems it will reach, what information it will see, what it will do to them, and the load or interruption the system owner states those systems can bear. Attach the scope record for the planned test.

evidenceHint.en: Per-test scope record naming systems, information reached, intended actions and the owner's stated constraints

title.en: Agree the window, the permitted actions and the limits with each system owner

description.en: Settle with the owner of each system in scope when the test may run, what may be done, what must not be done, who to contact if service is affected, and who may stop the test. Have both the person carrying out the test and the system owner accept it before anything begins. Attach the accepted agreement.

evidenceHint.en: Agreement naming window, permitted actions, prohibitions, stop authority and contact, accepted by both parties

title.en: Record the access the test needs, on what basis it is granted and when it ends

description.en: For each person or tool taking part, record what access will be used — access already held, access granted for this test, or supervised access alongside a member of staff — what that access permits, and the date and time it ends. Attach the access record.

evidenceHint.en: Access record per participant showing what access is used, what it permits, and when it ends

title.en: Capture what was done on each system during the window

description.en: Retain, against the test record, an account of the activity carried out on each system in scope during the agreed window, sufficient to reconstruct it afterwards — whatever the organisation can produce, from the systems' own activity records to a step log kept by the participant and countersigned by an observer. Attach it to the test record.

evidenceHint.en: The activity account covering the audit window, filed against the test record

title.en: Withdraw the access used for the test when the window closes

description.en: At the end of the window, withdraw or return each access on the access record, including anything raised in passing during the test, and record what was withdrawn and the date. Attach the withdrawal record.

evidenceHint.en: Withdrawal record showing each access withdrawn and the date it was withdrawn

title.en: Check each system touched for anything the test left behind

description.en: After the window closes, check the systems in scope for accounts, changed settings, files, jobs or residual load left by the test, and confirm each is back as it was. Record what was checked, what was found and what was restored, raising anything outstanding with the system owner. Attach the post-test check record.

evidenceHint.en: Post-test check record listing systems checked, residue found and what was restored
